- Fix: the performance overlay once again reports unified audio cost and keeps it visible in its section legend.
- Tests: three S3K object-registry test classes no longer fail depending on which other tests share their JVM fork. `Sonic3kObjectRegistry.create` resolves the S3K zone set from the *globally loaded level* -- `getCurrentZoneSet()` answers `S3KL` only while `romZoneId < 0`, i.e. while no level is loaded -- so `TestS3kFlybot767Badnik`, `TestAizMinibossRegistry` and `TestS3kMgzSwingingSpikeBallObject` were passing only by the accident of no level being loaded before them. Surefire runs with `forkCount=4, reuseForks=true`, so any earlier test in the same fork that left an MHZ-DDZ level behind flipped the zone set to `SKL` and every S3KL-only factory returned a `PlaceholderObjectInstance`, which is exactly the observed failure. None of the three had any reset at all; they now carry `@FullReset` + `@ExtendWith(SingletonResetExtension.class)`, so the zone set they assert against is established rather than inherited. Verified across repeated full runs: all three are green in every run since, and two consecutive runs produced byte-identical failure sets where the count previously swung between 44 and 52.
- Fix: pausing no longer lets silent presentation frames accumulate in the speaker FIFO while the OpenAL source is halted. Repeated user-pause and focus-loss transitions are idempotent, so tabbing away and back cannot stack seconds of silence ahead of resumed music.
- Fix: final PCM speaker playback once again primes and maintains three 1,024-frame OpenAL buffers. The unified presentation sink previously started as soon as one buffer was available and only ever queued one buffer per game-loop update, leaving about 21 ms of audio ahead at 48 kHz; ordinary frame-time jitter could therefore starve OpenAL, repeatedly stop and restart the source, and produce crunchy clicks at each discontinuity.
- Fix: launching Sonic 1 levels containing multi-ring placements and spilling rings in Sonic 2 or Sonic 3 & Knuckles no longer intermittently crashes rewind capture. Reserved-slot child rings and lost-ring objects now receive the same stable rewind identity as objects added through the normal dynamic-object path before they publish collision responses.
- Perf: the solid path's per-player maps are sized for a team instead of for 21 entries. `IdentityHashMap`'s no-arg constructor expects 21 entries and allocates a **64-slot** backing table for it; the maps built in `ObjectSolidContactController.resolveCheckpointBatch` and `DefaultSolidExecutionRegistry` hold a leader plus its sidekicks and are constructed for every solid object every frame, so almost all of that table was waste. Sizing them makes `IdentityHashMap.init` -- which had become the single largest allocation site in the engine -- fall from 183 MB to 80 MB, and engine-wide allocation from 1310 MB to 1215 MB. Exceeding the hint is only a resize, never a correctness problem, so the change carries no behavioural risk; reuse-and-clear was considered instead and rejected, because `finishFrame`'s map is retained in `previous` past its frame and `resolveCheckpointBatch` runs object code that could re-enter it. Across the three allocation fixes in this line of work the engine now allocates 1215 MB where it allocated 1586 MB (-23%), with the 99th-percentile frame time down from ~0.40 ms to ~0.28 ms and steady-state collections down from 5 to 2 per measured window.
- Perf: playing a sound effect no longer deep-copies its SMPS sequence data. `instantiateCached` went through `freshSource`, which re-froze the cached source on every trigger -- cloning the sequence bytes, three `byte[256][]` tables, an `int[]` word table and 256 voices plus envelopes -- to produce an object byte-identical to the one already in the cache. The cached data is already a frozen snapshot and a frozen snapshot is immutable: its fields are assigned once in the constructor, `AbstractSmpsData`'s only two setters (`setId`, `setPalSpeedupDisabled`) are called by the SMPS loaders at load time and never during playback, and nothing writes into the arrays handed out by `getData` / `getVoice` / `getPsgEnvelope`. It is now shared. In a zone like CNZ, where bumpers and springs fire SFX continuously, this removed 140 MB of the 1450 MB allocated over 27,000 replayed frames (-10%) and cut the **99th-percentile frame time from ~0.40 ms to ~0.27 ms** -- the deep copy was a burst allocation landing on exactly the frames a sound started, which is the shape that produces an audible hitch on slower hardware. The per-instantiation DAC and static-config copies are deliberately kept, being outside the immutability argument. Every audio test passes and the replay trajectory digest is byte-identical.
- Perf: the solid path no longer allocates a `Map.Entry` per player per object per frame. `IdentityHashMap`'s entry iterator hands back a **new** object on every `next()` rather than reusing a cursor, so both `SolidCheckpointBatch`'s defensive copy (via `new IdentityHashMap<>(source)` → `putAll`) and `DefaultSolidExecutionRegistry.finishFrame`'s two nested `entrySet()` loops were producing garbage proportional to the level's solid-object count every frame. Both now use `forEach`, which walks the table directly, and an empty batch short-circuits to `Map.of()` -- the common case, since most objects resolve no contact on a given frame -- avoiding both the map and its unmodifiable wrapper. Measured over 27,000 replayed CNZ frames: entry objects 36 MB -> 2 MB, entry iterators 29 MB -> 0, and engine-wide allocation 1586 MB -> 1450 MB (-9%). The defensive copy itself is kept: the batch outlives the call that hands it a map, so trusting callers not to mutate it would trade a real correctness guarantee for two allocations. Replay trajectory digest is byte-identical either side.
- Perf: object collision boxes (`SolidObjectParams`) are interned rather than rebuilt on every query, completing the solid-path allocation work begun with the routine profiles. The solid system asks each solid object for its box several times per player per frame and 183 of the 220 construction sites built a fresh record each call, from values drawn from a small discrete set -- per-type constants, or a per-mapping-frame table. It was the largest single allocation source left in the engine at ~180 MB across 27,000 replayed CNZ frames; it is now **zero**. Together with the profiles, engine-wide allocation is down **24%** (2107 MB -> 1591 MB) with both hot record types eliminated entirely. As with the profiles this is garbage-collector pressure rather than frame time -- measured medians are unchanged at 0.117-0.125 ms, because at 145x realtime headroom nothing was waiting on the allocation. The new `SolidObjectParams.of(...)` keys an exact five-int comparison, never a bare hash, so two different boxes can never collapse onto one cached entry and hand an object someone else's dimensions; a hash collision, a cold table, or an object whose box genuinely varies every frame falls back to an ordinary construction. The 37 sites that already assigned to `static final` constants were deliberately left alone, since those allocate once at class initialisation and were never part of the problem. Behaviour neutrality was checked on the full suite and on the replay trajectory digest, which is byte-identical either side of the change.
- Perf: solid-routine profiles are interned instead of rebuilt every frame. The solid-contact path constructed a profile per solid object per player per frame -- and two of them, because `level.objects.SolidRoutineProfile.fromProvider` built the canonical record and immediately converted it -- from provider reads that almost never change. JFR attributed 357 MB of a 2107 MB allocation total to those two records across 27,000 replayed CNZ frames; both now allocate **zero**, taking the engine's total allocation down 17% (2107 MB -> 1748 MB). This is garbage-collector pressure, not frame time: the measured medians are unchanged (0.117-0.123 ms either side) because at 145x realtime headroom nothing was waiting on the allocation, so the value is fewer GC pauses and less jitter rather than a faster engine. The cache is keyed by an exact packed signature of the thirteen fields that define a profile -- twelve flags in the low bits, `monitorVerticalOffset` in the high 32 -- so it caches rather than freezes: a monitor that stops being solid, or a platform that flips to top-solid, computes a different key and gets the correct new profile, which `TestSolidRoutineProfileInterning` pins directly. It is sound only because the records are immutable and compared by value; nothing in the engine compares them by identity and no `IdentityHashMap` is keyed by one, both verified before the change. The table is thread-confined rather than shared, because a plain table racing across threads can expose a written key before its value is visible and hand back a mismatched profile, and this is accuracy-critical code; duplicate entries across threads are harmless since the records are value-equal. It is direct-mapped and always re-checks the stored key, so a collision or a cold table costs an ordinary construction rather than a wrong answer. Behaviour neutrality was checked on the full suite, including every trace replay: the failure set is unchanged apart from the known ordering-flaky registry tests, which pass in isolation.
- Tooling: a JVM benchmark harness, so "which Java runtime runs OpenGGF best" is a measurable question. `com.openggf.tools.TraceBenchmarkTool` replays a recorded trace headlessly with no pacing and keeps every frame's raw per-subsystem timings, reporting p50/p90/p99/p99.9/max per section rather than the live overlay's rolling means — the overlay's smoothing is right for a HUD and useless for a comparison, because the engine finishes a frame well inside its 16.6ms budget (so a paced run reports 16.6ms on every runtime) and because a mean erases the tail, which is exactly where runtimes differ. `--mode update` (default) measures physics, collision, object execution, and audio synthesis with no rendering; `--mode full` adds rendering, whose timings are dominated by the graphics driver rather than the JVM and are labelled a sanity check rather than a ranking. Each run hashes the trajectory it simulated into a digest: if two runtimes' digests disagree they did not execute the same work and the comparison is void, so `BenchmarkCompareTool` prints that in place of a conclusion instead of leaving a reader to notice. Iteration 0 is flagged cold and carries a frames-to-steady-state figure (measured across warmup and measured frames as one series, since the warmup is where the settling actually happens); later iterations run warm off a freshly rebooted session, and the comparison quotes the fastest warm pass, because desktop benchmark noise is additive and the minimum is the closest estimate of true cost. `scripts/bench-jvms.sh` runs a JVM × GC matrix from a single shared jar, interleaved (A,B,C then A,B,C rather than grouped per runtime, so thermal drift is not charged entirely to whichever ran last) and `taskset`-pinned. Supporting engine changes: `PerformanceProfiler` gained an optional raw-sample sink (one hook in `endFrame`, so every existing instrumentation site feeds the harness for free) and a switch separating per-section allocation counting from section timing — allocation tracking costs a JMX call inside every measured section and that call's cost is itself JVM-dependent, so leaving it on would read as a fake timing difference; `RecordingFrameDriver` accepts a step wrapper so headless replay reports the same section names a live `GameLoop` frame does; and the per-frame trace drive was extracted from `TraceCaptureTool` into a shared `TraceReplayDrive`, because a second tool hand-rolling those phase rules would eventually desync the way capture already did once. `MemoryStats`'s `com.sun.management.ThreadMXBean` cast is now guarded — per-thread allocation counters are a HotSpot extension, so the unconditional cast turned any non-HotSpot JVM into a hard startup failure, which is precisely the JVM this harness exists to run on. Design: `docs/architecture/designs/2026-07-27-jvm-benchmark-harness-design.md`.
- Fix: S3K hardware-timing traces now distinguish genuine held-counter lag/loading rows from the ROM's held-counter `loc_62CC` title-card object loop. - Feature: added a session-owned, rewind-safe hardware timing FIFO for ROM-backed work. Preparation advances only through integer budgets at canonical VInt, pre-main-loop, and post-object production boundaries; live play admits prepared jobs in FIFO order, while a narrow recorded capability can hold and release only matching prepared identities without supplying payload or progress.

- Fix: S3K spilled rings in the previous collision-response list now use the live Obj37 coordinates published by the preceding object pass. The engine previously read its generic pre-update cache, which was one pass older than the SST pointer dereferenced by `Touch_Loop`; standalone MGZ advances from frame 12486 to 13447 and complete-run MGZ from frame 9259 to 15520.
- Fix: S3K attracted rings now read Player 1's centre from the point where their own SST slot executes. A carrier in an earlier slot has already moved the player, while a later carrier has not; treating every attracted ring as though it ran at the same phase produced the wrong MGZ ring collection. Standard MGZ advances from frame 12486 to its next ring-count mismatch, while the complete-run frontier advances from frame 6295 to frame 9259.
- Fix: S3K collapsing bridges now clear their object-owned standing bit when `SolidObjectTop` hands a rider off to terrain. The engine previously retired only its generic ride owner, leaving `Check_CollapsePlayerRelease` to treat a player already grounded elsewhere as still bridge-owned and force an incorrect airborne release. Standard MGZ advances from frame 5164 to 12486 and sheds 152 trace errors; the complete-run frontier advances from frame 5550 to 6295, exposing a later ring-count divergence.
- Fix: AIZ Giant Ride Vines now read the runtime-owned `AIZ_vine_angle` word advanced by S3K's post-object `ChangeRingFrame` phase, instead of deriving the angle from the independently bootstrapped level frame counter. The word advances by the ROM's `$180` step, participates in rewind through the existing combined animation adapter, and restores the standalone AIZ trace frontier from frame 2696 to frame 2707.
- Fix: S3K sidekick flight auto-recovery now publishes the delayed `Pos_table` Y directly, matching `Tails_FlySwim_Unknown`, while Sonic 2 retains its `Water_Level_1-$10` clamp through a typed per-game sidekick CPU rule. This advances the AIZ complete-run frontier from frame 14880 with 1707 errors to frame 25039 with 28 errors.
- Fix: act-transition object-manager rebuilds now preserve the numeric phase of the global V-int-derived Lost Ring floor-check cadence instead of subtracting one while separately marking the phase as inherited. The previous adjustment skipped the ROM's next scheduled floor probe after AIZ1 handed off to AIZ2; preserving the clock phase advances the AIZ complete-run frontier from frame 9376 to frame 14880 and reduces release-blocking differences from 1726 to 1707.
- Fix: folded ICZ swinging-platform child solids now expose their adjacent object-order `Status_Push` sample to `TailsCPU_Normal` only when that sample actually carries Push. This preserves the ROM's delayed d4 branch without replacing its delayed input word or synthesizing stale push state, advancing the ICZ complete-run frontier from frame 6117 to frame 13517 and reducing errors from 1,324 to 1,323.
- Fix: S3K horizontal invisible hurt blocks now use the ordinary `HurtCharacter` lost-ring owner timing instead of forcing their Obj37 owner to defer `Ring_count` clearing. The shared slot scheduler still defers naturally when the allocated owner is genuinely behind the live `Process_Sprites` cursor, advancing the ICZ complete-run frontier from frame 3175 to frame 6117.
- Fix: ICZ path-follow platform subtype 0 now derives its alternating one-pixel jitter from the runtime-owned `V_int_run_count` phase instead of assuming that the object-update counter is always one tick behind. This preserves normal gameplay's zero offset while honoring the independent V-int low-bit phase established at legacy replay starts, advancing the ICZ complete-run frontier from frame 3102 to frame 3175.
- Fix: restored ICZ complete-run snowboard controllers now retain the ROM-owned startup control, mapping-frame ownership, and object-control bits until `Obj_LevelIntroICZ1`'s native 30-tick timer expires, instead of skipping the startup routine and releasing its latches at title-card exit. On expiry the later controller SST now only clears `object_control`; it no longer duplicates motion already performed by the earlier player slot, so ordinary movement resumes on the next player dispatch. Together these corrections advance the ICZ complete-run trace frontier from frame 0 through frame 28 to frame 3102.
- Fix: S3K automatic tunnels now apply the final path velocity on the `loc_2970A` exit-transition frame; non-rolling angled landings publish Walk unless the native spindash flag is live; and LBZ tube elevators reproduce their full-solid offset geometry and action-before-player-checkpoint ordering. Together these advance the LBZ complete-run frontier from frame 2856 to frame 3009 and reduce comparison errors from 8,790 to 6,613.
- Fix: S3K automatic tunnels now model their word-sized position writes without erasing the player's 16:16 fractional words, and tunnel capture writes the Roll animation without manufacturing `Status_Roll`. This advances the LBZ complete-run trace from frame 2816 to frame 2856 and reduces comparison errors from 9,041 to 8,790.
- Fix: MGZ/LBZ smashing pillars now preserve `SolidObjectFull`'s grounded lower-half squash-edge semantics: when the overlap escapes into the side-contact path, the ROM sets `Status_Push` even if the player is moving away from the pillar face. The behavior is owned by the pillar's solid profile and advances the LBZ complete-run trace from frame 2270 to frame 2816 while reducing comparison errors from 9,291 to 9,041.
- Fix: LBZ rolling drums now relinquish their tumble-mapping ownership when movement selects a non-walk animation, allowing the native `$FE` Roll script to publish its mapping while the drum continues to supply negative `flip_type`/`flip_angle`. The shared player animator follows the ROM dispatcher boundary: only the `$FF` walk/run control path can enter `Anim_Tumble`; non-walk scripts remain authoritative. This advances the LBZ complete-run trace from frame 1707 to frame 2270 and reduces its comparison errors from 9,297 to 9,291.
- Fix: LBZ rolling drums now preserve the mapping published by the earlier player SST slot on the capture pass, then derive each active-ride tumble pose from the previous drum pass's `flip_angle` before publishing the next angle. The later drum slot no longer repeatedly overwrites the animation ID. This advances the LBZ complete-run trace from frame 1659 to frame 1707 and reduces its comparison errors from 9,309 to 9,297.
- Fix: LBZ1's ground-launch controller now models the ROM's full `object_control` animation ownership. The buried 30-frame hold uses `$03`, suppressing `Animate_Sonic`/`Animate_Tails` and preserving the established visible pose; the launch changes control to `$01`, so the spring animation's mapping is first published on the following native player dispatch. A seamless-handoff CPU follower whose live animation predates the LBZ controller publishes that carried pose once before the hold freezes it. This advances the LBZ complete-run trace from frame 0 to frame 1659.
- Fix: S1 run-chain terminal tails now follow recorder-owned manifest metadata instead of a game-wide title-screen assumption. Short level movies can declare `level`, completion movies can declare `title_screen`, and captures stopped before true movie exhaustion omit the endpoint. The Lua and native S1 recorders now stamp schema version 3.18 with byte-parity coverage; the committed GHZ maze chain replays its 232-row level tail, while a fresh full-completion capture was verified across its 10,943-row title-screen tail. MZ1 slot regressions now use the canonical native bootstrap, retaining fourteen blocking green guards and moving the remaining frame-3101 Lost Ring lifetime mismatch into the explicit `trace-diagnostics` lane.
- Tooling/Fixtures: both S3K BizHawk trace recorders' `ADDR_VBLA_WORD` moved from `0xFE12` to `0xFE0E`, fixing the physics.csv `vblank_counter` column. `0xFE12` is `Life_count` — the ROM's on-screen lives counter, occupying the high byte (`lives << 8`), changing only on a 1UP or death and holding just 2-4 distinct values across an entire multi-hour capture. `0xFE0E` is the correct address: the low word of the free-running `ds.l V_int_run_count` at `0xFE0C`, which ticks once per real VBlank (including lag and title-screen frames) and is the same address the S1 (`v_vblank_word`) and S2 (`Vint_runcount+2`) recorders have always read — S3K's recorders were the one holdout, each carrying its own copy of the constant since the six-recorder fleet has no shared address table (`tools/bizhawk/SHARED_MODULE_HANDOFF.md` §1-2). Fixed in both `s3k_trace_recorder.lua` (`LUA_SCRIPT_VERSION` 6.31-s3k → 6.32-s3k) and `s3k_complete_run_recorder.lua` (6.32-s3k-completerun → 6.33-s3k-completerun); the native C# port's `S3KRam.VblankWord` follows in lockstep. All 39 committed S3K fixture directories were regenerated over their existing, untouched `.bk2` movies: 35 carry the `vblank_counter` column and now read a live counter instead of the stale lives byte (offsets, row counts, and every other physics/aux cell reproduce exactly — `aux_state.jsonl` is byte-identical everywhere, since no aux field ever read that address); the 4 special-stage-profile directories are metadata-version-only. Every native differential gate (`S3KTraceDifferentialTests`, `S3KCompleteRunSegmentsDifferentialTests`, `S3KRunModeDifferentialTests`, `S3KCompleteRunDifferentialTests`) is retightened against the regenerated fixtures, including the legacy identity-(B) `runs/s3-knux-multibonus-ss/` run tree, which stays byte-identical (zero normalization) through this recapture. Measured effect on `TraceExecutionModel.deriveSonic3kPhase`'s vblank-fallback clause (reached only when both `gameplay_frame_counter` and `lag_counter` fail to advance): it decided **zero** rows across all 35 vblank-carrying fixtures before this fix and **5,673** after, with `hcz_completerun` alone accounting for 2,091 of them — two orders of magnitude above every other fixture, as predicted from the dead-address analysis. Every S3K trace-replay frontier held across all 15 replay classes: identical first non-camera divergence frame/field and identical pass/fail tallies, though per-class total error counts shift a little either way as previously-masked rows reclassify (`TestS3kAizTraceReplay` 3256 → 3258, `TestS3kCnzTraceReplay` 9115 → 9220) or clear outright — `TestS3kMgzTraceReplay` sheds 2,584 stale errors (10,768 → 8,184) at the unchanged f5164 `air` frontier (see `docs/status/trace-frontier-log.md` for the full before/after table). Two named assertions in the input-latch policy family flipped on the now-truthful counter: `TestTraceExecutionModel.sonic3kMissingCpuExecutionHookMarksMovingDuplicateAsLag` went RED → GREEN (its subject rows had `Life_count` frozen, masking the clause; the live column now advances as the test always claimed), and `TestTraceReplayStartPositionPolicy.preLevelPrefixInputEdgeWithoutStateAdvanceOnlyConsumesMovieInput` is a new RED — its qualifying-row precondition (all three counters pinned) held for exactly one row across all 39 fixtures under the dead address and zero under the live one, so the test's premise no longer holds and it needs re-authoring rather than a counter fix (see `docs/status/trace-frontier-log.md`). This was a capture-correctness fix — no `src/main/` file changed, so it cannot move any engine or trace-replay result on its own; the frontier movements above are the fixture data becoming honest, not an engine regression or improvement.
- Fix: a live recording started on the master title screen keeps its audio after the player enters a game. The previous entry carried the recording's audio lease across the backend swap, but entering a game rebuilds the presentation twice, and the first rebuild is not the backend swap: `Engine.exitMasterTitleScreen` runs `resetForGameplayFromMasterTitle` — and its `AudioManager.resetState()` — before `initializeGlobalGameplayServices` installs the real backend. `resetState` still retired the lease outright, so the recording was already dead by the time the carry could apply and the reported `IllegalStateException: Live capture audio handle is no longer attached` was never actually removed; the recorder degraded to phase-correct silence, logged one warning for the whole session and recorded a silent audio track. A mode transition rebuilds the presentation, it does not end a recording of the window, so `resetState` now marks the lease for rebind on the same terms as a backend swap. Only `destroy()` — the genuine teardown — retires it. Separately, a lease can no longer be carried onto a producer running at a different sample rate: a recording is muxed at the rate captured when it started (ffmpeg `-ar`), so following the producer across a rate change would write pitch-shifted audio that looks like it worked, and the rebind threw `IllegalArgumentException: snapshot clock rate does not match this clock` out of the presentation builder — a crash reachable from most of `AudioManager`. The lease is now retired with a warning naming both rates, and no failure escapes the rebind. `TestLiveCaptureSurvivesBackendSwap` asserts against the PCM the recorder is actually handed, driven by a real music source through a real producer, because its previous frame-count assertion passed identically whether audio flowed or not.
- Fix: a live recording started before entering a game no longer loses its audio the moment gameplay begins. Entering gameplay installs the real audio backend, which rebuilds the presentation producer, and the rebuild retired the recording's audio lease outright; the next frame failed and the graceful-degradation path answered with phase-correct silence, so the recording did not fail, it just went silent for good. A backend swap replaces the output device and is not a reason to stop recording what the engine is playing, so the lease is now carried across the rebuild with its clock phase and frame totals intact. A genuine teardown still retires it.
- Tooling/Fixtures: `s3k_trace_recorder.lua`'s `ADDR_FRAMECOUNT` moved from `0xFE08` (`Debug_placement_mode`, dead-zero in normal gameplay) to `0xFE04` (`Level_frame_counter`), bumping `LUA_SCRIPT_VERSION` 6.30-s3k → 6.31-s3k. This is the STANDARD S3K recorder's counterpart to `6564667eb`, which fixed only `s3k_complete_run_recorder.lua`'s copy of the same constant and missed this one because each of the six BizHawk trace recorders carries its own copy of its ROM address constants (see `tools/bizhawk/SHARED_MODULE_HANDOFF.md` §1-2 for the full cross-recorder audit and the still-queued sibling defect, `ADDR_VBLA_WORD` reading `Life_count` instead of the real VBlank word in both S3K recorders). The three canonical STANDARD fixtures — `traces/s3k/aiz1_to_hcz_fullrun/`, `traces/s3k/cnz/`, `traces/s3k/mgz/` — were regenerated on the fixed recorder: `physics.csv`'s `gameplay_frame_counter` column and every aux `vfc` / `oscillation_state.level_frame_counter` go from a constant `0`/`0000` for the fixture's entire length to a live, ROM-plausible value (monotonic apart from documented lag-frame stalls and level re-init clears); offsets and row counts are unchanged (511/20798, 3171/42253, 2602/35912) and every other physics/aux cell is byte-identical. The native C# port's recorder-identity fork over this address (`S3KAuxEventEngine.FrameCounterAddressFor`, the 4-argument `S3KTraceCsvWriter.FormatRow` overload, the split `S3KRam` frame-count constants) is deleted — both S3K recorders now read `S3KRam.LevelFrameCounter` (`0xFE04`) unconditionally — and `S3KTraceDifferentialTests` is retightened against the regenerated fixtures rather than loosened: the `"6.28-s3k"`/`"6.30-s3k"` version allowance and the MGZ-only `pre_trace_osc_frames` line allowance are both deleted, so the only permitted `metadata.json` delta is `recording_date`. Measuring the three S3K release-slice frontiers against the newly-live counter shows all three first-divergence frames holding exactly where they were on the dead-zero data (AIZ f2696 `x_speed`, CNZ f185 `y_speed`, MGZ f5164 `air`) — this was a capture-correctness fix, not an engine regression — while surfacing one true test-harness bug, fixed separately below.
- Tests: focused trace-replay scenario tests now drive frames through the same `TraceReplayFrameClosureDriver` the whole-trace comparison loop uses, via a new `AbstractTraceReplayTest.driveScenarioReplayFrame`. `TestS3kAizTraceReplay` previously carried a private stepper that special-cased only `VBLANK_ONLY` and let `ADVANCE_ONLY` fall through to a full level tick, so every `ADVANCE_ONLY` row ran a non-ROM level tick that advanced the object/VBlank/oscillator clock on a frame the ROM never ran — the opposite of the established `ADVANCE_ONLY` suppression contract. Those ticks land in the AIZ plane-intro prefix and shift the entire 20k-frame AIZ1 object phase, so every frame-exact scenario assertion downstream inherited the shift; 14 of the 16 AIZ scenario assertions (Giant Ride Vine grab/handoff, hollow-tree capture/camera/sidekick cadence, AIZ2 reload camera lock and sidekick gates, miniboss arena lock, Rhinobot contact frame) go green. Harness fidelity only: `replayMatchesTrace` is unchanged at 3,256 errors with its first divergence still at frame 2696, because it was already driving correctly.
- Feature: `capture.toggleKey` now carries its own modifiers. It defaults to `SHIFT+O`, and writing `CTRL+SHIFT+O`, `META+O` or a plain `SCROLL_LOCK` works as written — the Shift used to be hardcoded in the engine, so the binding claimed to be "the key" while the shortcut was really Shift plus that key, and there was no way to change or remove the Shift. Modifiers are matched exactly: a binding with no modifier does not fire while one is held. An existing `capture.toggleKey: O` is migrated to `SHIFT+O` automatically, so Shift+O keeps working with no user action.
- Change: if you had customised `capture.toggleKey` to something other than `O`, it is deliberately left as you wrote it and now fires **without** Shift, because guessing that you meant `SHIFT+<your key>` would silently rewrite a value you chose. Add `SHIFT+` yourself to restore the old behaviour.
- Known limitation: a bare `O` is a reserved value for `capture.toggleKey`. The migration that rescues existing installs matches on the value rather than on a schema version, so it re-runs on every launch and rewrites every spelling of an unmodified `O` — `O`, `GLFW_KEY_O`, `KEY_O`, `79` and the quoted `"79"` — back to `SHIFT+O`. To bind the toggle to a single unmodified key, pick a different key.
- Fix: `capture.toggleKey: "79"` is migrated like every other spelling of the superseded default. The quoted raw key code is a documented binding form and was the one spelling the migration missed, so a config written that way kept a bare `O` bound — which started a recording and toggled the object-debug overlay on the same unmodified keystroke, the collision the migration exists to prevent.
- Fix: unbinding a shortcut with `-1` now unbinds it. `-1` is the value the shipped config already uses for the unbound player B and C buttons, but a binding read as a chord (today `capture.toggleKey`) substituted its registered default for it — so the shortcut kept firing on `SHIFT+O` while the same binding read as a key code reported it switched off.
- Fix: a debug overlay toggle no longer fires on a keystroke another shortcut has claimed, so `Shift+O` starts a recording without also toggling the object-debug overlay and `Ctrl+P` copies the performance stats without also toggling the performance overlay. Only the exact chord bound to the same key stands the toggle down — a modifier held for an unrelated reason does not, because player two's jump defaults to right Shift and a blanket "no modifier held" rule would switch all sixteen overlay shortcuts off for as long as player two held jump (and likewise for the Shift held for debug fast movement). The claim follows `capture.toggleKey`, so rebinding it moves which keystroke is reserved.
- Docs: the recommended "bare key, no modifier" example for `capture.toggleKey` is no longer `P`. `P` is the hardcoded performance-overlay toggle and is checked before the debug-shortcuts gate, so following the example started a recording and left the performance overlay on screen for its whole duration.
- Docs: the per-binding modifier table no longer claims a chord on a chord-unaware binding never fires. The modifiers are dropped and the bare key is kept, so `debug.playback.toggleKey: "CTRL+P"` binds plain `P` — Ctrl+P does nothing and an unmodified `P` fires the shortcut.
- Docs: a separator-only binding such as `"+"` or `"++"` is no longer documented as unbound. `+` is the chord separator, so such a value names no key — but that makes it an *unresolvable* value, which falls back to the binding's registered default rather than unbinding. A player who wrote `capture.toggleKey: "+"` to switch recording off still had it live on `SHIFT+O`. Only `""` unbinds.
- Fix: a key binding written with a modifier — `"CTRL+SHIFT+O"` — is now understood instead of being reported as an invalid key and silently replaced by the default. Bindings without a modifier are unaffected and still resolve exactly as before.
- Fix: rewind and movie playback now reproduce the Alt and Super/Command keys the same way they already reproduced Shift and Ctrl. Alt was read from live hardware even while recorded input was driving the engine, so a shortcut using Alt behaved differently on replay than the identical shortcut using Ctrl. The reachable case is the special-stage debug keys during a visual trace session: they are read through a "no modifier held" check inside the window where recorded input drives the engine, so Shift and Ctrl came from the recording while Alt and Super came from whatever the keyboard happened to be doing, and a modifier held live could silently swallow a recorded keystroke. BK2 movies record no modifier column at all, so all four read as released under BK2 playback.
- Fix: keyboard shortcuts no longer stop working after switching windows with the Super/Command key. A key was forgotten only when its release arrived, and the release for the window-switch modifier goes to whichever window took focus — so the modifier stayed held forever and every shortcut that requires no modifier held (the playback controls, the recording menu, the trace picker, and the debug keys) silently stopped responding. Held keys are now dropped both when the window is left and when it is returned to, so a release swallowed by a minimise or by a window manager's own Super shortcut is recovered from on the way back in. The Super/Command key is also now recognised as a modifier, which is what lets a binding ask for it.
- Fix: `Ctrl+P` is not a dead keystroke, and does not touch your clipboard unless you asked for debug shortcuts. The performance overlay toggle stands down for `Ctrl+P` so the two do not fire together, but the stats copy it stands down for is a debug capability behind the `debug.viewEnabled` gate, which ships as `false` — so on a default install the reserved keystroke did nothing at all. The toggle now stands down only while the copy can actually run: with debug shortcuts off, `Ctrl+P` toggles the performance overlay exactly as it always did; with them on, it copies and does not toggle. The copy stays behind the gate rather than being promoted above it, so a shipped install never has a keystroke that silently overwrites the OS clipboard.
- Fix: the stats copy requires the **left** Ctrl. `Ctrl` in a chord means either Ctrl, and right Ctrl is player two's default Start — so in a two-player session, player two holding Start while player one pressed `P` overwrote the system clipboard with a performance dump. Right Ctrl+`P` toggles the overlay, as it did before the shortcut was expressed as a chord.
- Fix: unbinding `debug.keys.debugMode` (or `debug.keys.frameStep`) with `""` no longer makes every other unbound shortcut fire from the gamepad. An empty binding resolves to `-1`, and so did the unbound debug-mode binding it was compared against, so one press of the pad's debug-mode button fired every binding that was switched off — including all nine `debug.playback.*` keys, which ship unbound.
- Fix: the same for a *held* key, not just a pressed one. Unbinding `rewind.liveKey` with `""` made every other unbound binding read as held for as long as the gamepad's rewind bumper was down, because both sides of the comparison were `-1` — and player one's B and C buttons ship unbound, so they were read through that path and gained a phantom hold with no matching press. A negative key code is now rejected by both the held and the pressed accessor rather than by individual callers, so an unbound binding is off through every call site.
- Feature: the bundled configuration template is written to `config.yaml.example` beside the player's `config.yaml` on every run. A `config.yaml` holds the values a player changed and never regains the comments, new keys, or worked examples the template gains later; the example file keeps the current documented template readable next to it. The player's own `config.yaml` is not touched.
- Docs: `capture.scale` is documented as trace-capture only. Live viewport recording captures the game viewport at its current on-screen size, which is what keeps menu and debug-overlay elements that scale outside the game's pixel space in the recording, and is why resizing the window ends a live recording.
- Feature: `capture.container` sets the recording file extension (default `mkv`), so a recording can be written straight to MP4 rather than remuxed afterwards. ffmpeg selects its muxer from it; MKV plays every codec the engine offers, while MP4 is portable only with h264/h265 video and aac audio.
- Feature: the recording codecs are configurable. `capture.codec` selects `ffv1` (default), `h264` or `h265` — all three lossless — and `capture.audioCodec` selects `flac` (default), `aac` or `mp3`, the latter two lossy and marked as such where they are configured. H.264 and H.265 encode RGB directly rather than the conventional `yuv444p`, which is lossless in the codec's colour space but does not return the submitted pixels. `capture.ffmpegPass1Args` and `capture.ffmpegPass2Args` replace either ffmpeg pass outright for anything the codec keys do not cover; leaving the second empty skips muxing and records video only. `capture.codec` was previously parsed and then never reached the encoder, so selecting a codec silently did nothing.
- Fix: tests clean up the temporary files they create. `Files.createTempDirectory`/`createTempFile` calls put a directory or file in the system temp directory that nothing ever removed, leaving roughly 1,800 behind per full run; where that directory is a RAM-backed tmpfs they accumulated across runs until the filesystem was full, which then broke unrelated features that legitimately need temporary space. Tests now use JUnit's `@TempDir` or a self-cleaning helper, a guard test keeps new ones from appearing, and Maven points the test JVM's `java.io.tmpdir` at `target/test-tmp` so anything still missed is bounded and removed by `mvn clean`.
- Fix: a live recording no longer writes its lossless intermediate to the system temp directory. The phase-1 FFV1 video and raw audio are the same order of magnitude as the finished file, and on Linux `/tmp` is routinely a RAM-backed tmpfs a fraction of the disk size, so a long recording died partway through with no space left. Both now sit beside the final file, in the output directory the user already chose to receive something that large.
- Fix: a failed live recording now reports what ffmpeg actually said. ffmpeg's diagnostics were read and discarded to keep its pipe drained, so when it exited the engine saw only its stdin turning into a closed stream and reported `ffmpeg write failed ... Stream closed` -- hiding the real cause, such as `No space left on device`. The last few lines of ffmpeg's output are now attached to the failure.
- Fix: building an input handler without a configuration no longer leaks a temporary directory per call. Every no-argument `InputHandler` took this path and nothing ever removed the directories, so a full test run left one behind per construction; on a machine with a RAM-backed `/tmp` these accumulated into hundreds of thousands of directories and filled the filesystem, which then broke unrelated features that legitimately need temporary space. One directory is now created per process and removed on shutdown.
- Feature: an interrupted live recording now says so. A recording that ends for a reason the player did not ask for — the window being resized, or a capture failure — replaces the red-dot/`REC` indicator with a red `REC STOPPED: RESIZED` or `REC STOPPED: ERROR` notice in the same corner for three seconds. Previously the indicator simply vanished, which was indistinguishable from pressing the toggle, and a capture failure reached only a log line. Stopping the recording yourself, and ordinary shutdown, stay silent. The notice is window-only on the same terms as the indicator: neither the MKV nor an F12 screenshot contains it.
- Proved zero-allocation warmed presentation and clock-continuous mixed/silent FLAC media.
- Added final-PCM integration and ROM-backed source/toggle/rewind parity coverage.
- Fix: the live-recording controller no longer discards its audio handle when a release is refused for being issued off the audio producer's owner thread. The engine deliberately keeps the lease so a later stop can complete the release, but the controller threw away the only reference able to retry it — so the producer kept copying every presented packet into an orphaned lease and every subsequent recording in the process was refused and degraded to silence.
- Fix: a live-recording release refused because it was issued off the audio producer's owner thread no longer retires the engine's view of the lease. Previously the refusal still cleared it, so the producer kept copying every presented packet into an orphaned lease, the next recording attached a second one instead of being rejected, and a retry from the correct thread was a silent no-op — repeated start/stop cycles eventually exhausted the capture capacity. Live recording now follows the same rule offline capture already did.
- Fix: a rewind reverse-release now performs every step that can fail before the one irreversible step that ends the reverse session, and completes the release if a later step fails. Previously a failure after that point was reported as retryable, and the retry re-prepared an audio restore the ended session could no longer commit — leaking every voice the preparation had recreated and leaving the ring-alternation, command-cursor and donor-sound-binding state unpublished.
- Fix: shutting down the engine now releases the process-global engine reference. It was published at construction and never taken back, so a shut-down engine stayed globally reachable and the trace-teardown and rewind-release retry paths could still hand control to a master title screen belonging to a dead engine.
- Fix: tearing down the audio presentation now retires the offline capture lease and the live recording lease under the audio lock by one rule — each reference is dropped exactly when the audio producer accepts the detach. A teardown refused because it was issued off the producer's owner thread leaves both leases held and retryable, instead of letting the next capture attach a second lease to a producer that still holds the first; a teardown that fails after the producer has already released its leases drops both, instead of refusing every later recording with a handle that is already dead.
- Removed the temporary deterministic-runtime and live-recording lease switches superseded by unified presentation audio.
- Fix: a refused offline capture release (attempted off the audio producer's owner thread) no longer leaves an orphaned capture lease attached to the producer while the engine believes it holds none, which previously let a later recording attach a second lease instead of rejecting it.
- Fix: offline trace capture now records at the rate the presentation producer is actually clocked at, so a requested capture frame rate the engine cannot honour (for example a PAL region pinned to 50 fps) no longer truncates or zero-pads every captured audio packet, and a recorder that fails to open no longer leaks the capture lease for the rest of the process.
- TraceCaptureTool and TraceCaptureSession now capture the same final SMPS/WAV/PCM packets as live recording.
- Live recording now continues with phase-correct stereo silence when its audio tap is unavailable or fails.
- Made every presented frame choose one explicit forward, silent, or reverse audio mode.
- Preserved durable music when rewind cleanup finds no stale override to pop.
- Made OpenAL a bounded final-PCM sink so toggling recording cannot remove music, rings, or effects.
- Proved unified voice snapshots, FM/PSG user masks across restored music and later standalone SFX lifecycles, complete PCM-history rollback, and rewind cursors with an exact producer-clock reference renderer while legacy output remained uninterrupted.
- Added a continuously ticked inaudible presentation shadow to prove command order and shared live/headless outer-frame ownership before speaker migration, with legacy-matched region/chip settings, isolated restore callbacks, cross-game donor coordination ownership, and failure-safe command mirroring.
- Unified SMPS, fallback WAV, pitched SFX, and collision-safe raw SEGA PCM command resolution while retaining audible legacy output during migration; legacy S3K music and SFX keep one private coordination-counter owner.
- Fixed late live-audio capture attachment to inherit producer packet phase without inheriting pre-attachment frame totals, preserving exact fractional cadence during forward and rewind presentation.
- Centralized final-PCM cadence, silence, history, reverse playback, crossfade, and phase-exact non-consuming capture taps in one producer.
- Added bounded frame-boundary audio commands and deterministic voice admission without dropping structural state.
- Preserved SMPS music, SFX arbitration, DAC, and continuous effects as one composite presentation voice.
- Added deterministic WAV and raw-PCM decoding, interpolation, looping, pitch, and cursor restoration.
- Began consolidating audible sources behind an allocation-free software presentation mixer.
- Fix: live viewport recording now hot-attaches its deterministic audio tap only for the recording lifetime, preserving normal LWJGL playback before and after capture. Ongoing music/SFX are rebound without restarting, synthesized speaker PCM is handed back without a stop gap, reverse ownership is retained until rewind release, and non-timeline SEGA PCM commands remain audible and recordable.
- Feature: configurable live viewport A/V recording toggles with `Shift+O` by default, producing lossless FFV1/stereo-FLAC MKV files in `capture.outputDir`. Capture is limited to the fixed game viewport, finalizes automatically on viewport/resize changes and ordinary engine shutdown, and preserves synchronized forward, silent pause/frame-step, and reverse-rewind presentation audio without consuming speaker output. The window-only red-dot/white-`REC` indicator and F12 screenshots remain outside the recorded frames. This requires `ffmpeg` on `PATH` and is separate from the Shift+F9 input/movie recorder.
- Tooling: the native headless GPGX harness now records full canonical Sonic 3 & Knuckles STANDARD traces, replacing `s3k_trace_recorder.lua` (v6.30-s3k) for S3K capture on Linux across all three of its profiles — default `gameplay_unlock`, `aiz_end_to_end` (records its arm frame as trace row 0), and `level_gated_reset_aware` (discard-and-re-arm on soft reset, finalizes on zone-leave) — selected with `--trace-profile`; `--mode trace` now auto-detects the S3&K locked-on ROM alongside S1/S2. Three ROM-backed differential tests (`S3KTraceDifferentialTests`) gate byte-parity against the canonical AIZ end-to-end, CNZ, and MGZ fixtures: `physics.csv`/`aux_state.jsonl` byte-identical with zero normalization, `metadata.json` differing only in `recording_date` plus the documented `lua_script_version` 6.28-s3k → 6.30-s3k delta (and, MGZ only, its leftover `pre_trace_osc_frames` line). The 13 hook-driven aux event families (`OGGF_TRACE_ENABLE_DIAGNOSTIC_HOOKS`) remain deferred — pinned absent by `S3KHookAbsenceTests` — and the CLI now refuses every Lua environment variable that would silently change output the native port does not model (hook-arming vars, polled-family window overrides, and the two early-stop vars), rather than producing a quietly non-canonical capture. `s3k_complete_run_recorder.lua` (per-zone-segment/bonus/special-stage capture) is a separate, still-Lua-only migration; `--run-id`/`--gameplay-segment` are rejected on the S3K ROM.
- Fix: trace replay bootstrap now seeds `LevelManager`'s level frame counter from the trace row immediately before the first driven row, matching that field's documented contract (it holds the PREVIOUS completed level frame, because ROM increments `Level_frame_counter` before `Process_Sprites`, and 16 consumers recover the current value with `getFrameCounter() + 1`). It previously seeded the first driven row's value, running every frame-counter-keyed object phase exactly one frame ahead of ROM for the whole segment — invisible while the S3K complete-run recorder sampled a dead-zero address, and surfacing only once that column was captured live. The sibling sprite-counter seed three lines above already used the correct row. Effect on the mega-run chain against the regenerated fixtures: seg0 returns from 22,216 errors to 21 and the chain frontier returns to the seg2 exit boundary, with the AIZ Giant Ride Vine grab at f1934 (`object_control` 0x00→0x03, ROM seats the player at handle_y + $14) no longer attaching a swing-frame early.
- Fixtures: the canonical `traces/s3k/runs/s3-knux-multibonus-ss/` run (25 segments + `run_manifest.json`) is regenerated from `s3k_complete_run_recorder.lua` v6.32-s3k-completerun on Linux, replacing a 2026-07-19 Windows capture that predated the current recorder by three versions. The regenerated set is LF-only (was CRLF), stamps `6.32-s3k-completerun` throughout (level and special-stage segments and the manifest were `6.31`), and carries a live `gameplay_frame_counter` / `vfc` / `level_frame_counter` — the pre-`6564667eb` capture read `0xFE08` (`Debug_placement_mode`), dead-zero for the whole run, and reported `pre_trace_osc_frames: 0` from that same address. It also drops the 212 diagnostic-hook aux lines four segments carried from an armed-hooks capture (hcz_2 95, hcz_6 48, mgz 69, mgz_3 69). Segmentation is unchanged: identical offsets and row counts for all 25 segments, every physics cell outside the counter column byte-identical, all three special-stage segments byte-identical outright, and the manifest byte-identical apart from its version line. This makes the run byte-reproducible by the current recorder.
- Tooling: the native headless GPGX harness now records full canonical Sonic 3 & Knuckles COMPLETE-RUN traces, replacing `s3k_complete_run_recorder.lua` (v6.32-s3k-completerun) for S3K complete-run/bonus/special-stage capture on Linux — `--trace-profile complete_run` emits a per-zone segment directory (`physics.csv`/`aux_state.jsonl`/`metadata.json`) for every zone a playthrough movie clears, using the recorder's own ROM-derived zone tokens, and `--run-id` (mirroring `OGGF_TRACE_RUN_ID`) forces `run_manifest.json` emission and records bonus-stage (`s3k_bonus_stage`) and special-stage (`s3k_special_stage`) detour segments, published as one all-or-nothing no-replace set like the S1/S2 run ports. This completes the migration of the ENTIRE Lua recorder fleet (S1, S2, S3K standard, S3K complete-run) to the native harness. Three ROM-backed differential gates prove the port across the three known capture identities: `S3KCompleteRunSegmentsDifferentialTests` reproduces all seven committed `*_completerun` fixtures byte-identically from one untruncated complete-run pass over the 466,334-row canonical movie (plus a full 15-segment layout assertion and a no-manifest assertion); `S3KCompleteRunDifferentialTests` and `S3KRunModeDifferentialTests` together reproduce all four committed bonus/special-stage fixtures (`bonus_gumball`, `bonus_slots`, `bonus_pachinko`, `special_stage`) byte-identically under `--run-id s3k-multibonus`, and reproduce the whole `runs/s3-knux-multibonus-ss/` tree (25 segments + manifest) under `--run-id s3-knux-multibonus-ss` byte-identically — `physics.csv`/`aux_state.jsonl` by raw length and sha256 with zero normalization and `run_manifest.json` raw with no free field at all. That gate previously asserted only the tree's *structure*, with three independently pinned, non-byte-exact deltas (CRLF vs LF-only, the pre-fix `ADDR_FRAMECOUNT` `0xFE08` vs the current `0xFE04`, and armed-vs-deferred diagnostic hooks on four segments), because the fixture then in tree was a Windows capture from a Lua build three versions behind; regenerating it at v6.32 on Linux with the hooks off removed all three at the source, and the corresponding normalizations are deleted from the gate rather than left dormant. The same tightening applies to `S3KCompleteRunPublicationTests`' `run_manifest.json` formatter gate. `metadata.json` differs from the byte-exact fixtures only in `recording_date` — no version-line delta, since both sides stamp `6.32-s3k-completerun`. The 14 hook-driven aux families remain deferred exactly as for the STANDARD recorder — `S3KHookAbsenceTests`' old (B) counter-gate, which pinned the four then-hook-bearing run segments (`hcz_2`, `hcz_6`, `mgz`, `mgz_3`) as DOING carry hook events so the absence gate could never silently widen to them, lost its subject in the regeneration and is replaced by absence coverage of those same four segments — and the CLI refuses every complete-run-recorder environment variable that would silently change output the port does not model, with a test pinning the deliberately-not-refused set (including `OGGF_S3K_TRACE_PROFILE`, which this recorder never reads).
- Tooling: the native headless GPGX harness now records full canonical Sonic 3 & Knuckles STANDARD traces, replacing `s3k_trace_recorder.lua` (v6.30-s3k) for S3K capture on Linux across all three of its profiles — default `gameplay_unlock`, `aiz_end_to_end` (records its arm frame as trace row 0), and `level_gated_reset_aware` (discard-and-re-arm on soft reset, finalizes on zone-leave) — selected with `--trace-profile`; `--mode trace` now auto-detects the S3&K locked-on ROM alongside S1/S2. Three ROM-backed differential tests (`S3KTraceDifferentialTests`) gate byte-parity against the canonical AIZ end-to-end, CNZ, and MGZ fixtures: `physics.csv`/`aux_state.jsonl` byte-identical with zero normalization, `metadata.json` differing only in `recording_date` plus the documented `lua_script_version` 6.28-s3k → 6.30-s3k delta (and, MGZ only, its leftover `pre_trace_osc_frames` line). The 13 hook-driven aux event families (`OGGF_TRACE_ENABLE_DIAGNOSTIC_HOOKS`) remain deferred — pinned absent by `S3KHookAbsenceTests` — and the CLI now refuses every Lua environment variable that would silently change output the native port does not model (hook-arming vars, polled-family window overrides, and the two early-stop vars), rather than producing a quietly non-canonical capture. (S3K complete-run capture is now natively ported too — see the entry above.)
- Tooling: `s2_trace_recorder.lua` v9.13-s2 run mode now survives in-level reloads (death/star-post restarts, time overs, act and zone transitions, the SCZ→WFZ→DEZ ObjB2 routes) instead of finalizing the whole run at the first title-card reload, recording them as new `death_restart`/`level_advance` manifest transitions — `TraceRunManifest.ENTRY_KINDS` accepts the two new kinds — and run-mode special-stage segments now emit the hook-free subset of `s2_ss_trace_recorder.lua`'s aux event stream (frame −1 `state_snapshot`, `control_state`, `checkpoint`, `stage_finished`, `message_state`, `results_started`) into their previously empty `aux_state.jsonl`. Output is byte-identical to v9.12-s2 for all previously-capturable shapes apart from that documented aux superset.
- Tooling: the native headless GPGX harness mirrors the v9.13-s2 S2 run-mode extension — `Game_Mode $8C` reload survival with the `death_restart`/`level_advance` pending-transition lifecycle, the hook-free special-stage aux event stream (`S2SpecialStageAuxEventEngine`), `9.13-s2` version stamps, and a run-mode-only `--effective-movie-length` flag for capture sessions whose movie-length signal differs from the BK2's file-derived row count. - Tooling: the native headless GPGX harness now records full canonical Sonic 1 complete-run and run-mode traces, replacing `s1_complete_run_recorder.lua` for S1 capture on Linux: `--trace-profile complete_run` emits a per-level segment directory (`physics.csv`/`aux_state.jsonl`/`metadata.json`) for every level of a single playthrough movie, and `--run-id` (mirroring `OGGF_TRACE_RUN_ID`) adds the always-on giant-ring special-stage detour machine's `ss` segments (`trace_profile s1_special_stage`) plus `run_manifest.json`, published as one all-or-nothing no-replace set. - Tooling: the native headless GPGX harness now records full canonical Sonic 2 traces in all three `s2_trace_recorder.lua` modes — plain `gameplay_unlock`, `level_gated_reset_aware` with `--gameplay-segment` selection, and `--run-id` run mode with the special-stage detour, per-segment output directories, and `run_manifest.json` — replacing the Lua recorder for S2 capture on Linux; `--mode trace` auto-detects S1 vs S2 from the ROM. This removes three non-ROM AIZ plane-intro object updates and advances the standalone AIZ frontier from frame 717 to frame 2707.
- Fix: The S3K recorder now derives every profile's input column from `bk2_frame_offset + trace_row`; the AIZ end-to-end fixture is canonically BK2-aligned with only its input column normalized, and obsolete replay-phase metadata is removed from the AIZ and CNZ fixtures.
- Fix: S3K trace replay now derives pre-level intro prefixes from recorded mode transitions and drives level-gated frame zero through the ordinary production lifecycle, removing legacy sidekick, object, oscillator, and seed-row compensation scheduling, bounding input-latch-only phases to the recorded prefix window, and keeping phase/oscillator scheduling independent of frame-zero position, speed, and state outcomes.

- Fix(s3k): Mantis now establishes its managed visual-child graph before the wait-offscreen handoff, keeping each parent's child identity and back-reference available for rewind restoration.

- **Fix(s3k): objects the player destroyed or collected before a star-post bonus stage now stay that way on return, instead of respawning fresh.** The ROM keeps `Object_respawn_table` across the star-post-bonus `Restart_level_flag` reload: the bonus entry sets `Respawn_table_keep=1` (docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:61930) and the reload's clear routines skip the respawn/ring tables while it is set (`sub_EB1A` :18564-18570; the `Object_respawn_table` handling gated at :37432-37434), so the live table survives. The engine rebuilt a fresh `ObjectPlacementController` (empty `remembered`) on the bonus-return `loadZoneAndAct`, dropping the table -- so, e.g., a monitor broken before the bonus respawned intact and solid, side-blocking the returning player as a phantom wall. Now the persistent respawn-remember state (`ObjectPlacementController.remembered` + `stayActive`, the engine's `Object_respawn_table` model) is captured at bonus entry (`GameLoop`, alongside the star-post activation mark) and re-established on the bonus-return reload via a new `PersistentRespawnState` snapshot (`ObjectManager.capturePersistentRespawn`/`restorePersistentRespawn`); spawn indices are stable because the return reloads the same zone/act. Not rewound (the bonus round-trip is not a rewindable window; consumed on the return reload before the first rewindable frame -- the placement `remembered` remains independently rewind-captured within a level). Root-caused on the `s3-knux-multibonus-ss` Knuckles run: a monitor at (0x2B38, 0x2D3) broken in seg0 (frame 3744, matching the recorded ROM break f3743) reloaded intact in the returning aiz_2 and walled the player at f231; the recorded object's code pointer is `Sprite_OnScreen_Test` (0x1B588), the inert broken-shell routine `Obj_MonitorInit` installs (:40471-40478). Drives `TestS3kMegaRunChain` seg2 from 11651 to 5968 comparator errors (the f231 wall is gone; the residual is downstream). Verified regression-free: seg0 stays 4, seg1 (gumball) 9, `TestS3kAizCompleteRunTraceReplay` 0, `TestS1GhzMazeRoundTripChain`, `TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain`, the four S3K bonus/special-stage replays, `TestS3kAiz1SkipHeadless`, and `TestCheckpointStateRewind` all pass. Follow-up in docs/status/trace-frontier-log.md: the death-respawn reload shares the same fresh-`remembered` gap (also `Respawn_table_keep`-governed in the ROM), scoped out until a death-respawn trace needs it.
- **Fix(s3k): a gliding or sliding Knuckles now passes through and breaks a monitor instead of being walled by it, matching the ROM.** `Sonic3kMonitorObjectInstance` modelled only the roll-animation exemption from the monitor's solid and touch gates. The ROM `SolidObject_Monitor_SonicKnux` (docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:40567-40573) also returns non-solid, and `Touch_Monitor.checkdestroy` (:20858-20866) also breaks the monitor, when the character is Knuckles and `double_jump_flag` is 1 (gliding) or 3 (sliding after gliding) -- the two gates test the identical state. Added a shared `isKnucklesGlidingOrSliding` predicate, gated on the `GLIDE` secondary ability so Sonic's insta-shield `double_jump_flag==1` (`InstaShieldObjectInstance`) never qualifies, wired into both `isSolidFor` and `onTouchResponse`. Live-play relevant; verified regression-free on the S3K trace canaries (`TestS3kMegaRunChain` seg0/seg1, `TestS3kAizCompleteRunTraceReplay`, gumball/pachinko bonus replays, `TestS3kAiz1SkipHeadless`).
- Test(rewind): new report-only CI guard `TestHelperStateRewindCoverageGuard` catches the "uncaptured helper state" gap class — a `final` plain-helper field on a spawnable object whose type carries mutable frame-varying scalar state but has no `RewindCodecs` codec (a future `FooGate`/`FooTracker`/`FooLatch` that neither matches the ad-hoc plain-state-holder name-suffix list nor implements `RewindStateful`, or a plain-state holder that a future non-codec field silently knocked off the compact in-place path). On a backward seek such a helper's fields are left stale while the object's own instance fields roll back. `RewindCoverageAnalyzer` gains `findUncapturedHelperStateFields`, wired as a third gap list on `ObjectCoverage`; per the guard's cardinal rule it decides "captured" with the **same** public predicate the compact capturer uses (`RewindCodecs.codecFor`) and honors `RewindPolicyRegistry.policyForAudit` (skipping TRANSIENT/DEFERRED/CAPTURED) exactly like the sibling final-scalar and object-ref lanes — so render helpers such as declared-type-`TRANSIENT` `PatternSpriteRenderer`/`PatternDesc` are correctly not flagged. Depth is one level at the object; deeper nesting is delegated to `codecFor`'s own recursion. Baseline (`src/test/resources/rewind/helper-state-coverage-baseline.txt`) starts EMPTY — the current codebase has no such gap, so any future violation fails the guard. `TestRewindCoverageAnalyzer` gains a positive (name-matching all-scalar plain-state holder → codec-captured → not flagged) and negative (un-codec'd helper carrying a mutable boolean → flagged) case. Report + guard only; no runtime rewind behavior changes.
- Chore(trace): trace-run tooling cleanup. (1) `TraceCaptureTool` now rejects a multi-segment trace run up front — `resolveTrace` guards each of its index/name/path resolution paths with `requireCapturable`, which throws a clear "trace run ... is not capturable; capture its segments individually" message instead of failing opaquely mid-capture (a run drives the engine through level->stage mode changes this single-scene capture pipeline does not follow). (2) `TraceCatalog.scanRuns` now also excludes a `synthetic/` game dir from run discovery via the same `isSyntheticSubtree` filter the level scan uses — defense-in-depth (a no-op today, since synthetic fixtures live under `synthetic/`, not `synthetic/runs/`). (3) Consolidated the "comparator frame base" reasoning that caused repeated off-by-one artifacts into one authoritative contract javadoc on `AbstractRunChainTest.attachReturnedLevelSegment` (initial cursor == first-compared trace-frame index == frames the transition already consumed == `cursorFrame - segmentOffset`; values enumerated per transition kind), with `attachInteriorComparator`, `handoffIntoInterior`, and its bonus/Option-B branch referencing it instead of re-deriving. Tests: `TraceCaptureToolArgsTest` gains run-rejected / ordinary-trace-passes cases; `TestTraceCatalogRunDiscovery` gains a synthetic-run-excluded case. No gameplay/engine runtime behavior changes.
- Fix(s3k): the AIZ ride-vine hold no longer pins the held player's animation byte to HANG2 (0x14) for the whole ride — once a player who grabbed the vine *while rolling* is carried onto the floor, the anim byte follows the ROM to Walk (0x00), while mapping frame and position stay vine-driven. ROM anim ownership: `Obj_AIZRideVineHandle` CheckGrab writes anim=$14 once (docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:46742) and the hanging hold only writes `mapping_frame`, never `anim` (`AIZRideVineHandle_HoldPlayer` :46607-46636), so anim stays $14 while airborne. On the first grounding, `Player_TouchFloor` (dispatch :24335, `character_id` branch to `Knux_TouchFloor` at :24339) runs the Knuckles landing body (label :32829), which clears `Status_Roll` and writes `anim=0` **only when `Status_Roll` is set** (roll gate `btst #Status_Roll`/`beq` :32833-32836; matching the Sonic body `Player_TouchFloor` :24344-24347); a not-rolling grounding leaves anim at $14 (the second, independent gate — `cmpi #$20,anim` at :32865-32867 — resets only the >=0x20 glide family, not HANG2), and `Status_InAir` is cleared either way (:32855). Because the hold never rewrites anim, a rolling grab latches Walk for the rest of the grab even if the vine lifts him airborne again; a not-rolling grab keeps HANG2. `Status_Roll` during the hold equals its grab value (object_control skips movement), so the fix gates on a captured `rollingAtGrab` rather than the engine's live roll flag. The swing branch (`AIZRideVineHandle_HoldPlayerSwinging` writes anim=0 unconditionally, :46656) also latches Walk so a swing→hang transition keeps 0. The engine's `AizVineHandleLogic.setPlayerHeldMode0` previously force-wrote HANG2 every hold frame. The two new latch booleans (`rollingAtGrab`, `walkLatched`) ride rewind keyframes automatically via the plain-state-holder codec (`State`/`PlayerState` end in "State" with all-scalar fields, so the owning object's `handle` field is captured in place) — `TestAizRideVineRewind` is extended to pin them through a capture→mutate→restore cycle, so a mid-grab rewind restores the latch instead of reverting to HANG2. Object-scoped in the shared `AizVineHandleLogic` (AIZ ride vine + giant ride vine + MHZ swing vine). Root-caused via per-frame instrumentation of the `s3-knux-multibonus-ss` Knuckles run: at seg0 f1934 Knuckles grabs the AIZ Giant Ride Vine rolling and the engine held anim=HANG2 through ~f2000 while the ROM dropped to Walk at f1947. Drives `TestS3kMegaRunChain` seg0 from 56 to 4 comparator errors (the remaining four are the separate f1570 glide-anim and f1766-1767 roll-terrain-follow roots, owned by the movement/glide lane). Open note (frontier log): the exact ROM dispatch of `Player_TouchFloor` while `object_control=3` nominally skips `Knux_Modes` is unpinned; the write + effect set are cited and match the recorded f1947 transition. Verified (explicit per-class trace runs, since the plain suite excludes `tests/trace`): `TestS3kAizCompleteRunTraceReplay` = 0 (a not-rolling Sonic+Tails vine grab correctly keeps HANG2), seg0 stays 4, the six S3K/S1/S2 stage comparators, `TestS3kAiz1SkipHeadless`, `TestS3kHczCompleteRunTraceReplay`, `TestS1GhzMazeRoundTripChain`, `TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain`, and the rewind coverage/torture/inventory suites all pass. `TestS3kMhzCompleteRunTraceReplay` fails identically on and off this change (4651 errors, first at f218 `tails_animation_id`) — a pre-existing base-drift frontier documented in docs/status/trace-frontier-log.md.
- Fix(s3k): Knuckles' walk animation now freezes its mapping frame while `Status_Push` is set (standing at rest against a solid), instead of continuing to advance the walk cycle. The Knuckles animation profile (`Sonic3kPlayerArt.loadKnuckles`) was missing `setPushUsesWalkSpecialHandler(true)`, so `PlayableSpriteAnimation`'s `$FF` walk handler never took the push hold-branch for Knuckles and kept re-publishing the walk script's next frame every tick. ROM `Animate_Knuckles`'s walk handler tests `Status_Push` and branches to `loc_17ECC` (docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:33124-33125), which decrements the reload timer and returns without republishing `mapping_frame` -- freezing the last-published frame -- exactly mirroring `Animate_Sonic`/`loc_12A72` (:24833-24834, 25180); only when its timer expires does it publish `AniKnuckles04` (the dedicated push script). Added the flag to the Knuckles profile, and modelled the one behavioural difference between the two push handlers -- Knuckles' reload shift is `lsr.w #8` (:33161) vs Sonic's `lsr.w #6` (:25193) -- via a new `pushDelayShift` field on `ScriptedVelocityAnimationProfile` (default 6, so Sonic/Tails/S2 profiles are byte-unchanged), set to 8 for Knuckles. Root-caused on the `s3-knux-multibonus-ss` Knuckles run: at seg0 (`aiz`) f638 Knuckles lands and stands against an AIZ rock (`AizLrzRockObjectInstance` slot 14, `Status_Push`=1, speeds 0); the ROM holds `mapping_frame`=7 through f645 then switches to 0xCF at f646, while the engine advanced 7->8 and stayed off. After the fix the engine holds 7 then switches to 0xCF, matching the ROM, and the whole downstream cascade (including what earlier looked like a separate f3793 `anim_id`=4 cluster) re-syncs -- `TestS3kMegaRunChain` seg0 drops from 168 to 56 comparator errors. Remaining seg0 divergences (engine HANG2/glide anim ids at f1948/f1570, a 1-frame y_speed swap at f1766) are distinct non-push roots left as follow-ups in docs/status/trace-frontier-log.md. Verified regression-free against the develop base (ae1605502): the full suite's failing set is identical before and after (26 pre-existing failures across 8 classes -- `TestS3kAizTraceReplay`, `TestS3kHczCompleteRunTraceReplay`, `TestS2EhzHalfpipeRoundTripChain`, `TestS3kCnzDirectedTraversalHeadless`, two source guards, the chain seg2->seg3 boundary); the six S3K stage comparators, `TestS1GhzMazeRoundTripChain`, `TestS3kAizCompleteRunTraceReplay`, and `TestS3kAiz1SkipHeadless` all pass.
