- **S1 SLZ3 boss stops dropping spikeballs after any rewind:** `Sonic1SLZBossInstance` cached its scanned seesaw references in a `List<Sonic1SeesawObjectInstance>` gated by a separate `seesawsScanned` flag; that flag (a captured scalar) survived a rewind restore as `true` on a freshly recreated instance whose cache list restarts empty (object-reference lists are not part of the default rewind field capture, so this boss is never in-place-reuse-safe), permanently blocking the lazy re-scan and leaving Robotnik unable to align a seesaw ever again. Fixed by gating the re-scan on `seesaws.isEmpty()` instead of the separate flag, making the cache self-healing regardless of restore path.
- **S1 LZ conveyor belt spawner no longer loses its platforms after a rewind:** added `Sonic1ConveyorState.Snapshot`/rewind capture-restore and a new `Sonic1ConveyorStateRewindAdapter`, registered via `Sonic1LevelEventManager.extraRewindAdapters()`. `Sonic1ConveyorState` (ROM `f_conveyrev`/`v_obj63`) is consumed across frames by the LZ conveyor spawner/platform objects but was never part of rewind coverage — the same "trigger platform" bug class as the S2 `ButtonVineTriggerStaticAdapter` / S3K `Sonic3kLevelTriggerStaticAdapter`. A rewind seek to before a conveyor spawner's first visit left its `v_obj63` dedup bit set, so the rewind-recreated spawner saw a stale "already spawned" flag and self-deleted without ever recreating its child platforms, permanently losing the belt.
- **S1 underwater breath timer, countdown-bubble cadence, and drowning-music cue now survive a rewind seek:** `DrowningController` gained `captureRewindState()`/`restoreRewindState()`, wired into `PlayerRewindExtra` and `AbstractPlayableSprite`'s rewind capture/restore. Previously `DrowningController`'s state (remaining air, per-second frame timer, countdown-bubble bookkeeping, and whether drowning music had started) was never captured at all, so a rewind seek left it completely unaffected by the target frame — the breath countdown and drowning-music cue could desync from the restored gameplay state. This is shared S1/S2/S3K code.
- **S1 LZ1 water current no longer pushes Sonic into a still-closed door:** `Sonic1FloatingBlockObjectInstance`'s LZ1 switch-3 door (ROM object 0x56, `fb_type==3`) now implements `handleLz1WaterTunnel()`, which was previously a stub left over from before wind tunnels were implemented. ROM (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/56 SYZ, SLZ Floating Blocks and LZ Doors.asm:219-243`) disables the LZ1 water current (`f_wtunnelallow`) every frame the player hasn't yet passed the still-closed door, and unconditionally re-enables it the frame the door's switch is pressed. Without this gate, the current pushed Sonic against the closed door indefinitely — a softlock.
- **S1 pinball bumper no longer computes its bounce direction from a stale, one-frame-late player position:** `Sonic1BumperObjectInstance.applyBounce()` now uses the player's position captured at the moment of the actual touch (`onTouchResponse()`) instead of re-reading it live inside the deferred `update()` consumption a frame later. ROM's `Bump_Hit` computes its `CalcAngle` from the SAME frame `React_Special` sets `obColProp` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/47 Bumper.asm:29-30`, `sub ReactToItem.asm:377-427`); the engine's `ObjectManager` architecture instead consumes the touch on the object's NEXT `update()` call, one frame after the position was sampled. A fast-moving player (e.g. one just launched by a spring, matching the reported SYZ spring-into-bumper loop) can cross clean through the bumper's Y position during that single deferred frame, causing the bounce to be computed from the wrong side and launched in the wrong direction entirely.
- **S1 hurt Sonic now regains control immediately off an up/down spring bounce, matching ROM's unconditional routine override:** `Sonic1SpringObjectInstance.applyUpSpring()`/`applyDownSpring()` now clear the player's hurt flag at the same point ROM writes `obRoutine(a1)=2` (Sonic_Control) unconditionally on every spring trigger (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/41 Springs.asm:96,203`), regardless of what routine Sonic was in beforehand. Previously a spring landing while hurt (routine 4) launched Sonic correctly but left `hurt` set, so D-pad and jump input stayed locked (`PlayableSpriteMovement.handleMovement()` gates all input on `isHurt()`) until a later grounded hurt-stop landing, instead of restoring control the same frame the spring fires.
- **S1 MZ glass block reflection no longer floats away from the pillar:** `Sonic1GlassReflectionInstance` (short-variant sync, subtypes 3-4) now resyncs its Y-reference from the parent glass block's CURRENT `obY` (`parent.getY()`) instead of its static spawn baseline (`parent.getBaseY()`), matching `Glass_Reflect34`'s byte-verified `move.w obY(a1),objoff_30(a0)` (`docs/s1disasm/sonic.lst` `BB5E: 3169 000C 0030`, source displacement `$0C` = live `obY`, not `$30` = the static `objoff_30`). The stale baseline displaced the reflection by up to `glass_dist` (0x90/144px) while the pillar sat untriggered, reading as "floating in mid-air"; the reflection now sits on the glass face with only the ROM's small oscillator shimmer. The oscillator formula itself (already byte-accurate) is unchanged.
- **S1 Yadrin's top spikes now hurt even while Sonic is attacking, gated on a real ROM-accurate hitbox region:** `Sonic1YadrinBadnikInstance.isSpikeRegionHit()` now replicates React_Yadrin's actual sub-hitbox check — a 24px-wide region offset 4px from Yadrin's leading edge (mirrored when facing right), gated on Sonic's react-hitbox bottom edge clipping <8px into Yadrin's top edge — instead of comparing Sonic's and Yadrin's CENTRE Y values against that same threshold. The old centre-based check almost never matched a real top-graze touch (whose centre-to-centre distance is closer to the sum of both hitbox half-heights), so a rolling Sonic landing on the spikes safely destroyed Yadrin instead of getting hurt (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/Sonic ReactToItem.asm:532-561`).
- **S1 Egg Prison capsule button no longer flashes forever after triggering:** `Sonic1EggPrisonButtonObjectInstance` now freezes its switch-flash animation the frame it is triggered and blanks (mapping frame 6) once the parent capsule leaves its explosion phase for animal-spawning, instead of toggling between its two flash frames indefinitely. ROM's Pri_Switch/Pri_Explosion/Pri_Animals are the same object slot: AnimateSprite stops running once the object leaves Pri_Switch, and `.makeanimal` explicitly sets `obFrame=6` to "delete switch by turning it invisible" (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/3E Prison Capsule.asm:81-137`).
- **S1 lamppost checkpoints no longer show a duplicated, X-offset ball after the twirl finishes:** `Sonic1LamppostObjectInstance.onTwirlComplete()` no longer forces the pole's mapping frame to the red (pole+ball) frame. ROM's Lamp_Finish (routine 4) is a plain `rts` — the pole's own frame is never touched again this act, and the twirl child is never deleted (the top-level Lamppost dispatcher has no out_of_range check), so only the twirl's own frozen orbit ball should be visible (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/79 Lamppost.asm:6-11,122-134`).
- **S1 MZ lavafalls no longer flicker at their landing spot on the frame they spawn:** `Sonic1LavaGeyserObjectInstance` now applies its `-0x250` lavafall start-height offset eagerly in the constructor instead of deferring it to the object's first `update()`, so the position is correct even when the object manager's `FindNextFreeObj`-equivalent slot allocation can't schedule that first `update()` in the same exec pass as `GMake_MakeLava`'s spawn. ROM's Geyser_Main falls straight through into Geyser_Action + DisplaySprite in the same pass that creates the object, so it never displays a lavafall head at its un-shifted (eventual landing) Y (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/"4C, 4D MZ Lava Geyser and Maker.asm":157-172`).
- **S1 special stage jump responds to any of A/B/C again:** `GameLoop`'s `feat: route gameplay through logical input` change (`e2472501f`) started forwarding special-stage input as raw Mega Drive A/B/C button bits (`InputActionMasks.toMegaDriveButtonBits`) instead of the old blanket `pressedButtons |= 0x70` on any jump-key press, but `Sonic1SpecialStageManager.processJump()` still gated on the engine-internal `INPUT_JUMP` bit (`0x10`), which only coincidentally matches the Mega Drive B-button bit. Jump silently stopped responding to A (the common default bind) and C. Fixed by checking the new `Sonic1Constants.SS_JUMP_BUTTONS` (`0x70`, any of A/B/C) to match ROM `SonicSS_Jump`'s `andi.b #btnABC,d0` — the same `& 0x70` pattern already used by `Sonic3kSpecialStagePlayer.updateJump()`.
- **Default ROM filenames now use simple project-root names:** `config.yaml`, runtime defaults, setup docs, trace runbooks, and BizHawk examples now expect `s1.gen`, `s2.gen`, and `s3k.gen` instead of GoodGen-style archive names. User-facing docs identify the expected S1/S2 revisions and all three ROMs by CRC32/SHA-1 for verification.
- **S2 MTZ3 is green: MTZ boss (Obj54) frame parity, shield orb (Obj53) lifecycle, and the S2 impatient-wait blink gate.** Five ROM-backed fixes replace the round-95/96 compensations: (1) Obj54's first execution frame is consumed as Obj54_Init (setup ends `rts`, no Boss_MoveObject; the engine boss ran one float frame ahead of ROM for the whole fight); (2) orb 0 reuses the Obj53_Init spawner slot (`movea.l a0,a1`), so its first orbit lands one frame after orbs 1-6; (3) the whole Obj54_AnimateFace hit reaction (orb-break flag, angry face, SubA entry, velocity writes) and the Obj54_Defeated transition are applied after the current routine's movement, replacing the partial pending-X-velocity-clear; (4) Obj53's break path runs the `bra.s +` Obj53_OrbitBoss/SetAnimPriority tail on the break-consumption frame, the removed `verticalAngle += 0x10` contraction fudge matches the ROM tilt tail (which never touches objoff_3B), attacked orbs expose collision_flags 0 immediately (Touch_Enemy_Part2 clears them in RAM), and BounceAround is gated on mapping_frame == $B via a faithful Ani_obj53 AnimateSprite port including CheckPlayerHit's player-hurt pop; (5) the MTZ boss is persistent so the Sub12 flee keeps opening Camera_Max_X_pos to $2BF0 off-screen (docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:322A2-32B64, 36444-36468, 67767-68110, 85110-85162). `TestS2Mtz3LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f14204 / 188 errors to green, completing the S2 level-select trace suite.
- **S2 Sonic's impatient-wait blink/get-up input gate (Obj01_MdNormal_Checks) is now modeled on plain terrain:** once the WAIT animation reaches anim_frame $1E, held directions first play Blink (or GetUp past $AC) while the grounded update is skipped, so input response lags by the ROM's 3 frames (s2.asm:36444-36468; BizHawk probe over MTZ3 f15295-f15330 showed Ctrl_1_Logical fresh, no Control_Locked/move_lock, and the anim byte at $0A during the dead frames). The gate is profile-data-driven (S2 Sonic only; S1/S3K have no equivalent) and scoped to non-riding stands: object riders keep the existing per-object stale-logical-input models, which encode the same freeze for CNZ ObjD5, MTZ Obj65/Obj6C, and the SCZ Tornado.

- **ICZ1 rewind boundary capture no longer crashes on the snowboard intro:** the ICZ zone-event sidecar now treats the live `IczSnowboardIntroInstance` handle as transient structural state, leaving the object's lifetime/state to ObjectManager rewind capture. `TestZoneEventRewindSchemaGuard` now rejects identity-table-dependent fields in scalar-only zone-event sidecars, and `TestSonic3kIczRewindRoundTrip` covers the exact live-reference capture path that previously threw while loading Ice Cap Zone Act 1.
- **VHS rewind tear bands can be disabled independently:** new `rewind.vhsTearBands` (default `true`); set `false` to keep the rest of the VHS rewind effect (scanline jitter, chroma bleed, tape dropouts, head-switch strip, wobble) without the scrolling tear bands. Also fixes band scroll position teleporting when switching rewind speeds: the scroll phase is now integrated CPU-side (`RewindScroll` uniform) so a speed change alters the scroll rate, not the position.
- **Live rewind gains speed modifiers, and the VHS tear bands are softer:** holding the new `rewind.liveHalfSpeedKey` (default Left Ctrl) with the rewind key rewinds at half speed (one engine step every other frame, slow-motion reverse audio); `rewind.liveDoubleSpeedKey` (default Left Shift) rewinds at double speed; both held cancel to normal, and the mirrored left/right variant of a configured modifier also counts. `RewindSpeedController` gains a held-speed multiplier fed through its fractional step accumulator (now active outside tape-coast mode too), so `currentSpeed()` reports the effective rate and reverse-audio resampling plus the VHS envelope pick the modifier up automatically; with tape coast enabled the multiplier scales the coast curve's output without compounding into the acceleration. The VHS shader's third tear band now fades in via `smoothstep(1.2, 2.0, speed)` — fully visible at double speed, no band pop at the crossover — and the picture-search bands are softened (in-band displacement ~25→~14 px, static 40%→25%, chroma kill full→70%, tear line 0.35→0.22, slightly narrower band) so gameplay stays readable through them.
- **Live rewind now presents an authentic VHS picture-search effect:** while the rewind key is held (and through a ~10-frame release tail), a new engine-owned post-process pass (`RewindVhsEffectPass` + `shaders/shader_vhs_rewind.glsl`) renders scrolling tear/noise bands (a third band appears at high tape-coast speed), per-scanline jitter, chroma fringing with mild desaturation, sparse tape dropouts, a bottom head-switching strip, and sub-pixel vertical wobble. The pass runs after the fade pass and before any user display shader, so CRT presets display the damaged "signal"; the post-fade `REWIND <frame>` HUD label stays crisp. Intensity follows a 4-frame-attack/10-frame-release envelope (`RewindEffectEnvelope`) that latches the last tape speed so bands keep scrolling through the release tail. The shader pipeline is prewarmed at GL init (no first-rewind compile hitch) only when both `rewind.liveEnabled` and the new `rewind.vhsEffect` (default `true`) are set; compile/apply failure logs one warning and disables the effect for the session without touching gameplay or the user's shader selection. `DisplayShaderPipeline` gains a per-frame dynamic-uniform `apply` overload.
- **S3K Madmole arc-throw arm now grabs the carried player on the ROM frame:** the SKL Obj $8C Madmole (`Obj_Madmole`, `docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:193075`) applied its arc-throw grab two frames late. Seven ROM-cited fixes in `MadmoleBadnikInstance`: (1) the body child performs its first `MoveSprite2` rise step on the creation frame because `loc_8D620` falls straight through to `loc_8D636` (`:193147-193158`); (2) a one-frame parent-observe gap precedes the 60-frame cooldown — the parent `loc_8D5D4` tests the still-set `$38` busy bit and waits on the frame the body clears it at `loc_8D6D6`, so `loc_8D5DE` arms the cooldown the next frame (`:193110-193120,193212-193215`); (3) the side-drill child sets `usesCurrentTouchResponseState = true` because `loc_8D6E6` moves the arm before `Add_SpriteToCollisionResponseList`/`Draw_Sprite` (`:193264-193278,193233`), so the next frame's touch reads the arm's post-move position (the same post-move Collision_response_list contract as AizSpikedLog/Orbinaut); (4) the arcing arm moves under `MoveSprite_LightGravity`'s `moveq #$20` gravity, not the `$38` object default (`:178358`); (5) the carry defers to routine 8 — `sub_8D94A` sets routine 8 during the arm's routine-4 `loc_8D778`, which still runs `MoveSprite_LightGravity` that frame, and `loc_8D7A8` carries the following frame (`:193271,193478,193291`); (6) the carry pins the player with subpixel-preserving word writes because `loc_8D7D4` does `move.w` to `x_pos(a1)`/`y_pos(a1)` only, leaving the carried CPU's `x_sub`/`y_sub` (F600/2E00) untouched (`:193307-193312`); (7) the grab targets a single player selected from a pending `collision_property` candidate — `sub_8D94A` indexes `word_8D944` = `{Player_1, Player_2, Player_2}` (`:193457-193460`), so the last player to overlap wins (Player_2 after Player_1) and the lead player is never modified. The new per-frame `pendingCapturePlayer` scratch is `@RewindTransient` (nulled at the start of every update before any snapshot boundary, so always null when captured; no rewind coverage baseline change). `TestS3kMhzCompleteRunTraceReplay` advances from frame 2966 (`tails_air`, 4454 errors) to frame 2986 (`tails_y`, 2413 errors); the grab now applies on ROM frame 2966 with the air/status/object_control/subpixel state and arm arc matching the ROM through f2985.
- **S3K TailsCPU now runs the `sub_13EFC` interact-code-word despawn watchdog:** the S3K sidekick CPU despawns Tails when, off-screen and standing on an object, the stood-on object's routine-pointer high word differs from the latched `Tails_CPU_interact`, matching `sub_13EFC`'s off-screen on-object `cmp.w (a3),d0 / bne` branch into `sub_13ECA` (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:26816-26843`, `26800-26809`). A new S3K-only `ObjectInteractionRules.sidekickDespawnUsesInteractCodeWordChange` gates the word-change compare in `SidekickCpuController.checkDespawn()` (S1/S2 `false`, S3K `true`); the compare runs before the fall-through latch refresh (ROM compare-then-latch) and is armed only when the latch is non-zero (a real object code high word is always `>= 0x0001`, and the reset paths zero the latch, so a captured word is never `0`). The despawn reuses the existing faithful `applyDespawnMarker` path (`x_pos = 0x7F00`, `y_pos = 0`, routine 2, `Status_InAir`, `object_control = 0x81`, velocity preserved per `sub_13ECA`), and no new rewind field is added — `diagnosticS3kInteractWord` is already captured/restored in the sidekick CPU snapshot. The stood-on object's ROM code word is exposed at the object boundary through a new `RomObjectCodePointerProvider` interface, implemented by `Mhz1CutsceneButtonInstance` (high word `0x0006`, `MHZ1CutsceneButton_Main` at ROM `0x00062F0A`, `sonic3k.asm:130055-130125`) and `MhzCurledVineObjectInstance` (high word `0x0003`, `loc_3E8A2` at ROM `0x0003E8A2`, `sonic3k.asm:82778-82797`); only objects that supply a code word participate, so the watchdog is data-driven, not zone-gated. In the MHZ complete-run this reproduces the ROM sequence where the button word `0x0006` is latched on-screen and a later off-screen landing on the `0x0003` curled vine mismatches, despawning Tails at f2159. `TestS3kMhzCompleteRunTraceReplay` advances from frame 2159 (`tails_x`, 2323 errors) to frame 2966 (`tails_air`, 4454 errors); an independent A/B rerun (6 files reverted to HEAD vs applied) confirmed the f2159 `tails_x = 0x7F00` sentinel target is eliminated, the f2159-2965 respawn window is byte-clean, and every remaining divergence record is at frame >= 2966 — the new first error is a separate, previously-masked root (ROM Tails goes airborne one frame before the engine while carried by moving object slot `0x15`), so the +2131 net is a wider live-sidekick cascade past the advanced frontier, not a pre-frontier regression. All six sibling S3K complete-run traces stay frame-neutral (AIZ f1095, CNZ f1846, HCZ f1489, ICZ f3139, LBZ f2270, MGZ f866); guards green including `TestS2Ehz1TraceReplay`, `TestS1Ghz1TraceReplay`, and `TestSidekickCpuDespawnParity` (55/55, six new fail-first cases covering the off-screen word-change despawn + velocity preservation, same-word survival, on-screen re-latch, unarmed-latch no-fire, and S3K-only rule gating).
- **S3K MHZ curled vine now lands players on the contoured curl surface instead of a flat surface at spawn.y:** `MhzCurledVineObjectInstance` now implements `SlopedSolidProvider` so new-landing detection samples the generated per-segment curl surface, not a flat top-solid at spawn.y. `getSlopeData()` encodes each 2px sample as `vineY - (segmentY[segment] - 8)` (baseline `0`) so the shared resolver's `baseY = anchorY - slopeSample` reproduces ROM `loc_3EA1E`'s (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:82980-82996`) `$1A(a2,d0*6) - 8` surface; `isSlopeFlipped()` returns `false` since the segment generator (`:82861-82893`) does no render-flag mirroring (h-flip is folded into the existing per-segment index instead, now shared between the landing sampler and `onSolidContact`). `onSolidContact` also now distinguishes the establishing frame from a continued ride: ROM gates the surface Y write on the per-player standing bit (`btst d6,status(a0)`, `:82943`) — clear on first contact falls through `loc_3EA1E` into `loc_1E45A` (`:42004-42028`), snapping `y_pos = surface - y_radius - 1`, one pixel higher than the continued-ride contour (`loc_3E9FA`, `:82963-82977`, `y_pos = surface - y_radius`). The engine previously applied the continued-ride snap even on the landing frame. `TestS3kMhzCompleteRunTraceReplay` advances from frame 2158 (`tails_y_speed`, 4388 errors) to frame 2159 (`tails_x`, 2323 errors). An independent A/B rerun confirmed zero divergence records before f2159 and an identical (37-field) error-field set between before and after, so the -2065 error delta is a genuine cascade collapse, not a masked regression; the next root is the un-modeled S3K TailsCPU watchdog respawn (`sub_13EFC`/`sub_13ECA`, `sonic3k.asm:26816`/`26800`), shared sidekick-controller code correctly left untouched here. Two new `TestMhzCurledVineObjectInstance` cases cover the sloped-landing discriminator and the establishing-vs-continued-ride Y distinction.
- **S3K MHZ swing bars now preserve the captured player's subpixels per the ROM word-only position writes:** `MhzSwingBarHorizontalObjectInstance` and `MhzSwingBarVerticalObjectInstance` swap 8 subpixel-zeroing `setCentreX/Y` calls to `set...PreserveSubpixel`, because every ROM position write in the swing-bar routines touches only the pixel word (`move.w`/`add.w`/`subq.w`/`addq.w` on `x_pos`/`y_pos`), never the long that would clear `x_sub`/`y_sub`. Sites (all verified word-only writes in `docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm`): horizontal grab `:83448-83450`, hang `:83533-83534`, and the LEFT/RIGHT input nudges `:83326`/`:83340`; vertical roll-radius Y correction `:83752-83754`, grab `:83757-83759`, climb `:83625-83626`, and auto-release `:83669`. Previously each captured player was resnapped with its subpixel fraction reset to `0`, which diverged the trace at frame 1994 (`y_sub` expected `0xA500`, actual `0x0000`). `TestS3kMhzCompleteRunTraceReplay` advances from frame 1994 (`y_sub`, 2621 errors) to frame 2158 (`tails_y_speed`, 4388 errors). An independent A/B rerun confirmed the fix's three subpixel targets (`y_sub@f1994`, `tails_y_sub@f2011`, `x_sub@f2451`) are eliminated and the replay is now byte-exact through f2157 (zero divergence records before f2158, vs 51 in BEFORE); the +1767 net is a previously-masked downstream Tails swing-bar release/riding-state root now reachable at f2158 (CPU Tails enters an air+rolling state while the ROM keeps him riding object slot 15), with every new divergence record at frame >= 2158 — not a pre-frontier regression. Seven new fail-first `TestMhzSwingBar{Horizontal,Vertical}ObjectInstance` cases assert the subpixel fraction survives each grab/hang/input/climb/auto-release/roll-radius site.
- **S3K MHZ1 cutscene door now moves on its trigger frame instead of deferring a frame:** `Mhz1CutsceneDoorInstance` now falls through into the movement step on the same frame a slide is triggered (both the switch-driven and auto-raise trigger branches), instead of `return`ing after arming the slide. `MHZ1CutsceneButton_Door_Move` (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:130237`) arms `y_vel`/`$2E`/`$34` and falls straight through `Door_SetVelocity` (`:130246`) into `Door_Moving` (`:130251`, `jsr MoveSprite2`) with no `rts` in that chain, and both trigger paths (the switch branch's direct jump and the auto-raise branch's fall-through from `Door_ClearFlag`) reach it — so the ROM door moves 1px on its own trigger frame. The engine previously lagged the ROM door by 1px through the whole slide, which at frame 1162 let the door's underside clip the rising CPU Tails jump apex instead of clearing it. `TestS3kMhzCompleteRunTraceReplay` advances from frame 1162 (`tails_y`, 2855 errors) to frame 1994 (`y_sub`, 2621 errors); an independent rerun confirmed zero divergence at or before f1162, so all five prior fix signatures hold. Four `TestMhz1CutsceneObjects` assertions and two down-slide loop counts were corrected to encode the trigger-frame move.
- **S3K MHZ1 cutscene door now uses the inclusive right-edge side contact its ROM path takes:** `Mhz1CutsceneDoorInstance` now overrides `usesInclusiveRightEdge()` to `true`. `MHZ1CutsceneButton_Door_Wait`'s `jsr sub_65E4C` (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:130214,134149`) reaches `SolidObjectFull` -> `SolidObject_cont`, whose right-edge X-window check is `cmp.w d3,d0 / bhi.w` (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:41399-41406`) -- `bhi`, not `bhs` -- so `relX == width*2` (a player resting exactly against the door's right edge) is still a valid zero-distance side contact, matching the sibling `Obj_MHZ1CutsceneButton`'s existing override. `TestS3kMhzCompleteRunTraceReplay` advances from frame 1025 (`status_byte`, 2853 errors) to frame 1162 (`tails_y`, 2855 errors); an independent A/B rerun confirmed the fix's own window (f1025-f1100) drops from 2 errors to 0 with no new errors introduced there, and the region through f1811 is byte-identical before/after -- the +2 net is downstream cascading redistribution in already-diverged `tails_*` state past the pre-existing f1162 frontier, not a regression. `TestMhz1CutsceneObjects#mhz1DoorUsesInclusiveRightEdgeForRestingSidePush` covers the new override.
- **S3K MHZ1 cutscene button top-landing width and solid anchor now match its ROM object data:** `Mhz1CutsceneButtonInstance` seats its solid box on the raw ROM `y_pos` and uses its own ObjDat `width_pixels` for the top-landing X gate. The ROM object stores the solid box on `y_pos` (trace slot 11 = `0x67C`), but the engine keeps `this.y = spawn.y() + 4` for the sprite draw, so the solid box was 4px low; the `SolidObjectParams` now carries `offsetY = -4` to shift the solid anchor back onto ROM `y_pos` without moving the render. Separately, `sub_65DEC` (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:134105`) passes collision `d1 = $1B` into `SolidObjectFull`, but `loc_1E154` (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:41611-41632`) re-reads `width_pixels(a0) = $80` (`ObjDat_MHZ1CutsceneButton`, `docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:134853`) for the landing X gate, so the standable window is the full `$80` half-width, not the `$1B` side box; `getTopLandingHalfWidth` now returns `0x80`. To support this, `ObjectSolidContactController.isWithinTopLandingWidth` now honors an explicitly-configured landing width that differs from the collision half-width in either direction (previously only a narrower configured width was honored, wider fell back to the `collision - $B` heuristic). This is behavior-preserving for every existing solid: all 14 current `getTopLandingHalfWidth` overrides return a value narrower-than-or-equal-to their collision half-width, so only the new button takes the wider path. `TestS3kMhzCompleteRunTraceReplay` advances from frame 966 (`y`, 2967 errors) to frame 1025 (`status_byte`, 2853 errors). Two new `TestSolidObjectManager` cases cover the rising right-edge graze getting the top-slice lift under a wider-than-collision landing width, and the default narrow width still rejecting the same graze.
- **S3K MHZ mushroom-cap bob counter no longer advances during the trace-replay VRAM warmup:** the S3K complete-run trace-replay bootstrap runs extra `Animate_Tiles` passes before the first compared frame purely to warm the ROM's pre-frame-0 VRAM tile state (`TraceReplaySessionBootstrap.advanceAnimatedTilePreludeForTraceReplay`). Every animated-tile channel except the MHZ mushroom-cap position counter recomputes its transfer from current camera/frame state, so the warmup reproduces the ROM's DMA output without side effects; the mushroom-cap channel is the one stateful accumulator, advancing `Anim_Counters+$F` by 2 (wrap at `$58`) per pass (`AnimateTiles_MHZ`, `docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:54901-54908`). That counter is already seeded to its ROM `LevelLoop` frame-0 value by the single pre-loop `Animate_Tiles` pass (`loc_6468`, `docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:7853-7855`), and the mushroom caps read it as their bob phase (`MHZMushroomCap_UpdatePosition`, `docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:82199-82221`); the ROM has no equivalent warmup, so any advance during the prelude is a harness artifact that left the caps two bob-steps (`+4`) ahead. `Sonic3kPatternAnimator.updateForReplayBootstrapPrelude()` now preserves the counter across the warmup so caps enter comparison at the ROM frame-0 phase. Replay-only path — fresh gameplay's per-frame `Animate_Tiles` (`Sonic3kLevelAnimationManager.update()`) is unchanged. `TestS3kMhzCompleteRunTraceReplay` advances from frame 72 (`y_speed`, 3615 errors) to frame 966 (`y`, 2967 errors). `TestS3kMhzPatternAnimation#mhzReplayBootstrapPreludeDoesNotAdvanceMushroomCapCounter` covers the preserved-across-prelude / advance-on-normal-update contract.
- **S3K MHZ1 camera/min-X now honor the ROM `Get_LevelSizeStart` level-load override:** `Sonic3k.loadLevelData` now sets a `boundariesMinXOverride` of `$C0` for MHZ Act 1 played as Sonic/Tails (Knuckles excluded), matching ROM `Get_LevelSizeStart` `loc_1BF1E`'s `Current_zone_and_act==$700`/`Player_mode<3`/`SK_alone_flag==0` special case, which overrides `Camera_min_X_pos`/`Camera_target_min_X_pos`/`Camera_min_X_pos_P2` to `$C0` and forces the initial `Camera_X_pos` up from MHZ1's plain `LevelSizes` `xstart=0` (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:38111,38214-38225,38246`). Previously the engine started MHZ1's camera unclamped at `playerCentreX-$A0` (`0x0039`) instead of ROM's `$C0`, diverging `TestS3kMhzCompleteRunTraceReplay` at frame 1 on `camera_x`; the trace now advances to frame 72 (`y_speed`), matching the pre-existing historical frontier recorded before this regression. `TestSonic3kMHZEvents#act1LevelLoadPinsCameraAndMinXToRomMhzStart` and `#act1LevelLoadKeepsLevelSizesMinXForKnuckles` cover the Sonic/Tails override and the Knuckles no-override cases.
- **MTZ boss spawn no longer NPEs without a loaded ObjectManager:** `Sonic2MTZEvents.spawnMTZBoss()` restores the null-guard that every sibling zone-event spawn site has — the reserved-slot spawn introduced by the MTZ boss slot-scoping fix called `levelManager().getObjectManager()` unconditionally, which threw in headless event-spec harnesses that drive `Sonic2MTZEvents.update()` without a loaded level. Production behavior is unchanged (a live gameplay session always has an ObjectManager); the reserved-slot spawn parity is preserved.
- **ARZ platform and CNZ Point Pokey P2 access migrated to `ObjectPlayerQuery`:** `ARZPlatformObjectInstance`'s all-players standing-latch scan now iterates `services().playerQuery().playersFor(ALL_ENGINE_PLAYERS)` and `PointPokeyObjectInstance`'s captured-sidekick index resolution reads `services().playerQuery().sidekicks()`, replacing raw `services().sidekicks()` access flagged by `TestObjectPhysicsStandardizationGuard`. Same participant set, no behavior change; capture/resolve stay index-consistent because both sides use the same query source.
- **Rewind now captures the S2 post-camera unload latch, restoring EHZ1 seek/replay determinism:** `ObjectManager.s2LatchedObjectManagerCameraX` — the latched post-camera coarse-X consumed by object-side MarkObjGone/MarkObjGone2 unload checks on the next RunObjects pass (introduced for ARZ2 Obj82 dust slot timing, `docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:5111-5112, 33033-33036`) — was not captured in `ObjectManagerSnapshot`, so a rewind `seekTo` left the latch at its later live-frame value and the first replayed frames unloaded objects against a future camera edge, permuting dynamic slot allocation (first seen as `TestRewindTorture#tortureFixedAdjacent` diverging at frame 1700 on an EHZ bridge-stake slot, plus cascading `gamerng.seed` divergence in the random-seed tortures). The latch now rides `PlacementSnapshot` alongside `twoAxisCameraYCoarse` (legacy snapshots default to `MIN_VALUE` = live-camera fallback). Regreens `TestRewindTorture`, `TestRewindIter1631Diagnostic`, and `TestRewindEncounterValidation#s2Ehz1MidRunTraversalMatchesAfterRewindReplay`.
- **fix(sidekick): Tails fly-in regression — root-crossing completion and missed landing after the CNZ2 object-control fix.** Commit `dcaa4cb3e` made `TailsRespawnStrategy.requiresPhysics()` dynamic (the S2 fly-in runs `Obj02_MdAir` object physics when `obj_control` bit 0 is clear, per ROM `Obj02_Control_Part2` `btst #0,obj_control(a0)`, `docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:38973`), which had two side effects on the shared controller paths that reused `requiresPhysics()` for a different question: (1) the multi-sidekick root-leader-crossing completion shortcut (guarded to physics-driven approaches by `0f1225ebb`) started firing for the S2 Tails fly-in, landing Tails into NORMAL against the human root leader instead of keeping it targeting its CPU chain leader; and (2) engine-owned SPAWNING entries without the despawn marker (level-transition bootstrap, focused tests) ran fly-in gravity that ROM's despawn cycle suppresses, leaving Tails grounded 4px below the recorded target so `TailsCPU_Flying`'s pre-move Y-residual test never hit zero and the fly-in never completed. Fixed by (a) a new `SidekickRespawnStrategy.approachMovementUsesPhysics()` predicate (default `requiresPhysics()`; Tails overrides `false`) now used for approach-leader resolution and the root-crossing completion gate, so the fly-in keeps its ROM homing/landing semantics even when the physics tick runs; and (b) `SidekickCpuController.setInitialState(SPAWNING)` establishing the ROM spawn-wait invariant `obj_control=$81` (every ROM path into the spawn-wait routine writes it: `TailsCPU_Despawn` s2.asm:39396-39406, the `TailsCPU_Flying` off-screen timeout s2.asm:39142-39157, S3K `sub_13ECA` sonic3k.asm:26800-26809), while `beginApproach` continues to preserve the live byte so a parked-Tails object write (e.g. CNZ tube release `loc_25036`) still yields the ROM physics-active fly-in. `TestMultiSidekickSpawn#testTailsFlyInDoesNotLandWhenCrossingRootSonicBeforeChainLeader` and `TestS2Ehz1Headless#testRegisteredTailsDoesNotStandStillForSecondsAfterFlyInLanding` return to green; the full S2 trace sweep holds 15 green / 4 expected-red (ARZ2 f2016/753, CNZ2 f9487/288, MTZ3 f13336/352, OOZ2 f9342/505).
- Basic startup/title/data-select screens now accept controller directions and face-button actions.
- Rewind and recording playback now inject logical input snapshots instead of fake key-code input.
- Gameplay and special-stage input now consume logical P1/P2 state, preserving Mega Drive A/B/C identity for special stages.
- GLFW gamepads now map D-pad/left-stick directions and west/south/east face buttons to Mega Drive A/B/C logical input (Xbox X/A/B, PlayStation Square/Cross/Circle).
- Keyboard input now feeds the controller-ready logical input layer while preserving the existing Space/Right Shift defaults.
- Add controller-ready input configuration keys, defaults, and deprecated jump-binding migration.
- Add logical controller-ready player input state for the controller support MVP.
- **`DefaultObjectServices` legacy 7-arg constructor removed (audit tier B):** the deprecated `GameServices`-reconstituting fallback constructor and its nine orphaned private `legacy*()`/`engineServicesFromGameServices()`/`requireActiveRuntimeForLegacyConstructor()` helpers are gone; the session-backed `(GameplayModeContext, EngineContext)` constructor is now the only public form. `BootstrapObjectServices` — the constructor's one real caller, via `super(...)` — now composes from `SessionManager.getCurrentGameplayMode()` + `EngineServices.current()`, keeping its fail-without-active-runtime contract (`IllegalStateException`). `TestObjectServicesMigrationGuard`'s 17 line-level `DefaultObjectServices` bridge approvals were retired (the class no longer touches `GameServices` at all) and `BootstrapObjectServices`' wildcard `GameServices.` approval narrowed to the two composition-boundary lines.
- **`PsgChipGPGX` renamed to `PsgChip`:** with the deprecated legacy `PsgChip` deleted (below), the sole PSG implementation takes the plain name. Class javadoc keeps the Genesis Plus GX provenance note; no behavior change.
- **Dead deprecated code removed (audit tier A):** deleted the unreferenced `@Deprecated` class `PsgChip` (superseded by the active `PsgChipGPGX`; even `TestPsgChipSnapshot` exercises GPGX) and the unreachable `SimpleDataSelectManager` (S1/S2 data select routes through `CrossGameDataSelectPresentations.donated(...)` to the S3K presentation — the stale CLAUDE.md fallback note was corrected in the same change). Also removed zero-caller deprecated members: `Camera.setLookUpBias()`/`setLookDownBias()` (superseded by the ROM-accurate incremental bias adjusters), `WaterSystem.loadForLevelS1()` plus its now-orphaned private S1 water-height/underwater-palette helpers and `Sonic1Constants` import (S1 water loads via `loadForLevelFromProvider`), and the two deprecated non-pooled `PatternRenderCommand` constructors (all callers use `obtain(...)`). `WaterSystem.loadForLevel()` (S2) was verified still live (`LevelManager` fallback + tests) and retained. No behavior change.
- **MHZ end-boss defeat fragments now scatter with the ROM-correct `Obj_VelocityIndex` velocities:** `MhzEndBossDefeatFragmentChild`'s `VELOCITIES` table used `Obj_VelocityIndex` rows 4-9; the ROM-correct rows are 2-7, since `Set_IndexedVelocity`'s `d0=8` base (`sonic3k.asm:179163-179177`) combines with `CreateChild6_Simple` (`sonic3k.asm:177119-177139`) seeding each fragment's raw ROM `subtype` byte as `0,2,4,6,8,10` (not `0..5`), giving an effective stride of `8 + spawnIndex*4` -- byte offsets 8,12,16,20,24,28 into `Obj_VelocityIndex` (ROM `0x0852F4`), not 16,20,24,28,32,36. Found and ROM-byte-verified (via `RomOffsetFinder --game s3k search-rom`, not just the disassembly transcription) during Task V1 MHZ parity-wave validation's Step 4 low-confidence spot-check. `TestMhzBossObjects#mhzEndBossFadeWaitUnderflowSpawnsRomDefeatFragments` now asserts the corrected per-fragment X/Y positions after one `Obj_FlickerMove` tick.
- **MHZ swing bars now reject a hurt or dead player's grab and play the vertical bar's ROM grab SFX:** `MhzSwingBarHorizontalObjectInstance.tryGrab()` and `MhzSwingBarVerticalObjectInstance.tryGrab()` now also reject the grab while the player is hurt or dead, matching `cmpi.b #4,routine(a1) / bhs.w locret_3EFB8` (horizontal, `docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:83439-83440`) and the equivalent `bhs.w locret_3F35E` check (vertical, `sonic3k.asm:83737-83738`) via the same `!isHurt() && !getDead()` predicate already used by `MhzSwingVineObjectInstance`/`MhzMushroomParachuteObjectInstance`. The vertical bar's grab now also plays `sfx_Grab` on capture, matching `sonic3k.asm:83775-83776`, which was previously missing. `TestMhzSwingBarHorizontalObjectInstance` and `TestMhzSwingBarVerticalObjectInstance` add hurt/dead grab-rejection coverage for both bars and a grab-SFX assertion for the vertical bar.
- **S3K MHZ small SFX/frame nits batch:** five focused ROM-fidelity fixes across MHZ objects. `MhzMushroomCatapultObjectInstance.launch()` now plays `sfx_MushroomBounce` once per launch call instead of once per rider standing on the launching cap, matching `sub_3FA5A`'s single shared `jmp Play_SFX` (`sonic3k.asm:84351-84352`). `MhzSwingVineObjectInstance` now plays `sfx_Grab` only on a fast grab (`x_vel >= $400`; the slow-grab path returns via the `object_control(a1)` guard before reaching `jsr Play_SFX`, `sonic3k.asm:47472-47494`) and now plays `sfx_GroundSlide` every SWINGING tick whose updated angle byte lands in the `$40`-`$47` band (`loc_226C2`, `sonic3k.asm:47056-47061`). `MhzMushroomCapObjectInstance`'s `ANIM_BOUNCE` script no longer carries an extra trailing idle-delay frame at speed 0, matching `Ani_MHZMushroomCap_Seq1`'s exact 23-frame length before its `$FC` terminator (`Anim - Mushroom Cap.asm:5-6`). `MhzEndBossWeatherVisualChild.SPARK_FRAMES` restores the dropped initial `$0D` frame (`{0x0D,0x0E,0x0F,0x10}`), matching `byte_769CE` (`sonic3k.asm:157786-157787`). `MhzMinibossEscapeShardInstance`'s priority buckets now match ROM: `INITIAL_PRIORITY_BUCKET` 4→6 (`word_75E7E`'s `$300`, `sonic3k.asm:156794-156795`) and `RETURN_PRIORITY_BUCKET` 2→3 (`loc_7594C`'s `$180`, `sonic3k.asm:156232-156234`).
- **MHZ swing-vine jump-off velocity now matches the ROM ×$C multiplier:** `MhzSwingVineObjectInstance` release-in-swing-mode now scales `cos(angle)`/`sin(angle)` by `$C` (12) instead of `<<3` (8), matching `loc_229B6`'s `asl.w #2,d1 / move.w d1,d2 / asl.w #1,d1 / add.w d2,d1` (and the identical sequence for `y_vel`), which computes `value*4 + value*8 = value*$C` (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:47311-47325`). The previous `<<3` launch was only 2/3 of the ROM's jump-off speed. `TestMhzSwingVineObjectInstance#fastGrabJumpReleaseUsesSwingVelocity` now asserts `x_vel == cos(angle)*$C` (`0x0C00` at angle 0, up from the prior `0x0800`).
- **MHZ mushroom parachute steering and wall collision now match ROM:** `MhzMushroomParachuteObjectInstance.updateAngle()` had the LEFT/RIGHT sign-correction conditions swapped, so the steering angle oscillated by 2 instead of sweeping toward $80/$00, leaving the parachute unsteerable; the two conditions are now flipped to match `sub_3F7E2` (LEFT forces the angle non-negative before `+2`, RIGHT forces it non-positive). The object also now ports `sub_3F7AE`'s two horizontal wall sensors (at the parachute's `x_radius` of `$20`), run after `SubpixelMotion.moveSprite2` applies the frame's velocity per `loc_3F51C`'s `sub_3F7E2 -> MoveSprite2 -> sub_3F7AE` order, so the parachute no longer clips through walls. The left-wall sensor push also now uses `x_pos -=` (matching ROM `sub_FD32`'s `sub.w d1,x_pos` and the existing Knuckles-glide `doGlideCollision()` asymmetry) instead of `+=`, which had pushed the parachute deeper into a left wall instead of out of it.
- **S3K MHZ Pulley Lift handles now spawn with zero extension:** `MhzPulleyLiftObjectInstance` no longer seeds `HandleState.offset` from the handle-writer's `$34`/`$36` immediates on construction; both handles now spawn at their implicit RAM-zero extension and only extend when the rider holds down. `Obj_MHZPulleyLift`'s init routine (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:82376,82393`) writes those immediates into the handle's own field `$36(a1)` — a parent-slot field-offset *selector* later read by `loc_3E4B6` (`$36(a0)`) to pick which parent field (`$34`/`$36`) mirrors the handle's own `$34(a0)` extension — not a seed for `$34(a0)` itself, which stays at its ROM RAM-zero default (`loc_3E472`, `docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:82514-82539`). The prior port confusion made both handles spawn pre-extended and visibly retract over several idle frames with a spurious frame-1 parent y_pos nudge; `TestMhzPulleyLiftObjectInstance` now covers zero-extension spawn, no parent y_pos nudge on frame 1, and stable held-player position across idle frames.
- **S3K MHZ CurledVine now contours the rider to the curved surface:** `MhzCurledVineObjectInstance` now writes the standing player's Y from the generated curl segment table every standing frame instead of leaving the rider flat at spawn.y, and its top-solid landing window is now the ROM's asymmetric `$40`-left-offset range instead of a window centred on spawn.x. This matches `Obj_MHZCurledVine`'s `loc_3E9FA` per-frame `y_pos(a1) = segmentY - 8 - y_radius(a1)` write and `sub_3E9C6`'s `0 <= (playerX - vineX + $40) < rangeWidth` acceptance window (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:82949-82977`).
- **MHZ StickyVine now applies the ROM `sub_3EC66` pull vector:** `MhzStickyVineObjectInstance` replaces its `sign(d)*clamp(|d|/2,1,4)` heuristic with the ROM's `GetArcTan`/`GetSineCosine` vector math over the full sub-pixel (x_pos:x_sub) delta to the anchor -- `x_pos -= cos(angle)*d3*4`, `y_pos -= sin(angle)*d3*2` while airborne, where `d3 = (|dxPixel|+|dyPixel|)*2` -- honouring the distinct air (position pull + conditional `x_vel` halving) and ground (`ground_vel` halving) branches. This corrects both the pull magnitude (previously a coarse 1-4px/frame snap; now a ROM-accurate sub-pixel pull) and the pull direction (previously axis-independent; now a true diagonal vector toward the anchor).
- **Madmole now leaves a solid cap stump instead of vanishing when defeated:** `MadmoleBadnikInstance.destroyBadnik()` no longer marks the whole cap+body object destroyed when the player defeats the emerged body. It now spawns the explosion/animal/points sequence on a freshly allocated slot, snaps the state machine back to the buried cap position (matching ROM `sub_8D876`'s SolidObjectFull cap collision, which never depended on body state), and latches a `bodyDefeated` flag that permanently suppresses re-emergence — modeling the ROM parent's `$38(a0)` bit 1 never clearing once the body is killed off the normal sink-delete path. The cap keeps its own SST slot and stays solid forever, matching ROM instead of both cap and body disappearing together.
- **MHZ1 cutscene switch door now spawns pre-lowered on a mid-act re-entry:** `Mhz1CutsceneDoorInstance` now adds the ROM `+$40` `y_pos` offset at init when its parent button's door-lowered latch (the engine model of ROM `_unkFAA9`) is already set at spawn, matching `MHZ1CutsceneButton_Door` testing `_unkFAA9` right after setting the fixed `$390,$620` door coordinates (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:130205-130212`). Previously a respawned door always started at the raised `$620` position even if the cutscene had already lowered it before death.
- **MHZ pollen landing-burst leaf angle now uses the correct RNG byte:** `MhzPollenSpawnerInstance` now seeds each burst-leaf particle's angle from the high byte of the `Random_Number` word (`(raw >>> 8) & 0xFF`) instead of the low byte, matching `loc_3DAD6`'s big-endian `move.w d0,angle(a1)` byte-field write before the low word is masked for `x_vel` (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm` ~81706). This only affects the leaf drift direction/speed on landing bursts during MHZ's autumn season.
- **S3K MHZ Dragonfly tail-return now ripples one frame per link instead of moving all at once:** `DragonflyBadnikInstance.LinkedBodyChild` now gates each linked-body segment's return-to-parent-Y transition on a `DragonflyHoverReturnGate` check of its own `followAnchor` (the previous segment, or the Dragonfly itself for segment 0) instead of always reading the main Dragonfly's hover-wait state. Each segment exposes a one-frame-delayed "return gate" value to its successor (promoted once per its own `update()`), reproducing the ROM's `loc_8DE8A` `btst #2,$38` ripple down the `parent3` chain without replicating `CreateChild4_LinkListRepeated`'s `AllocateObjectAfterCurrent` slot-reversal quirk that produces it (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:193858-193871,177038-177061`). A new `TestDragonflyBadnikInstance#sevenSegmentTailEntersReturnOneFrameApartDownTheChainNotAllAtOnce` drives a real 7-segment tail and asserts each segment enters return exactly one frame after its predecessor. A companion `wingFlapSequenceOverFiveHoverCyclesAlternatesUpDownOnToggledBit` test confirms `switchBodyAnimationAfterHover`'s existing `bchg`-style toggle already alternates `byte_8DFCE`/`byte_8DFC2` as UP,DOWN,UP,DOWN,UP across five hover-wait exits, matching `loc_8DDF8`; no wing-flap code change was needed.
- **MHZ swing vine and vertical swing bar now force the camera to ROM anchor coordinates:** `Camera` models the ROM `Scroll_force_positions` flag as a frame-scoped, coordinate-carrying request (`requestForcedScroll(forcedX, forcedY)`) that zeroes the horizontal scroll frame offset (`H_scroll_frame_offset`) and points the horizontal/vertical camera math at the supplied coordinates instead of the focused sprite for that frame, mirroring the existing `requestFastVerticalScroll()` `Fast_V_scroll_flag` pattern. `MhzSwingVineObjectInstance` calls it every swinging frame Player 1 is grabbed with the vine's own `x_pos`/`y_pos` (ROM `loc_226F2`, `sonic3k.asm:47072-47074`), and `MhzSwingBarVerticalObjectInstance` calls it every frame Player 1 is hanging with the bar's `x_pos` and `Player_1+y_pos` (ROM `loc_3F0CC`, `sonic3k.asm:83575-83577`). Previously both left the camera tracking the player with its normal deadzone/delay while the player hung. Consumer `loc_1BFB8` (`sonic3k.asm:38296-38300`).
- **MHZ end boss hit-flash palette parity:** `MhzEndBossInstance` now selects the real-color palette row on the final invulnerability-window frame instead of the white/flash row (the `btst #0,$20(a0)` parity in `loc_767E8` was inverted), so palette-line-1 indices `{4,10,11,13,14}` no longer stay stuck white after a hit.
- **MHZ miniboss raw-animation script `$F8`/`$FC` commands:** `MhzMinibossInstance`'s raw-animation script interpreter now implements the `$F8` (re-point script base by a signed relative offset, `loc_845E4`) and `$FC` (re-emit the frame/delay pair at the script base, `loc_845F2`) commands, so `FINAL_LAUNCH_SCRIPT` settles on frame `$06` after its jump and `FINAL_CAMERA_RISE_SCRIPT` loops back to frame `$00` instead of silently resetting the script offset and skipping a frame pair.
- **S3K MHZ2 end-boss background now uses the ROM's exact per-routine vertical deform selection:** `SwScrlMhz` now switches the BG vertical scroll factor to the `sub_554B8` formula, `(Camera_Y_pos_copy - $280) * 5/32 + $180`, for every `Events_routine_bg` value except `0` and `$C`, which stay on the standard `MHZ_Deform` base of `Camera_Y_pos_copy * 5/32 + $76` — not a flat `>= $8` cutoff, since routine `$C` (the `y>=$500` redraw phase) is numerically `>= $8` but ROM-unconditionally uses standard deform, while routine `4` (numerically `< $8`) is ROM-unconditionally `sub_554B8`. The branch reads `Sonic3kMHZEvents.isBossAreaBackgroundDeformActive()` through `MhzZoneRuntimeState`, not zone name, and the shift-based `computeBgY` math floors negative camera-Y deltas per ROM `asr.l` semantics rather than truncating division (`docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:112861-113104`). `SwScrlMhzTest#endBossVerticalDeformUsesSub554B8BaseWhenRoutineBgIsInBossAreaRange`, `#routineBg4UsesSub554B8Unconditionally`, `#routineBgCUsesStandardMhzDeformUnconditionally`, and `#sub554B8UsesAsrFlooringNotTruncatingDivisionForNegativeDelta` cover the exact routine mapping and the rounding edge case.
- **Per-game rule placement guidance now documents the smallest-owner path for ROM divergences:** new architecture guidance directs agents to use typed `GameRules` records for shared runtime rules and existing providers, profiles, registries, or object hooks for narrower data, zone, and object-family behavior instead of adding new broad rule bags.
- **BizHawk diagnostics now hide every EmuHawk-owned startup window:** the hidden launcher now enumerates all top-level windows owned by the EmuHawk process and hides them immediately, then polls aggressively during the first startup seconds. This closes the gap where BizHawk could surface a non-main or not-yet-stabilized WinForms window before the fast no-render Lua wrapper took over.
- **BizHawk diagnostics now keep EmuHawk hidden after startup:** the hidden launcher now starts EmuHawk without shell execution and continuously hides the main Win32 window while the fast Lua wrapper runs. This preserves the normal no-audio/no-render diagnostic mode even when BizHawk recreates or re-shows its WinForms main window after process launch.
- **S2 hurt recoil now clears roll-jump before setting airborne state:** `AbstractPlayableSprite.applyHurt` now mirrors the ROM hurt path's reset-on-floor tail by clearing `Status_RollJump` and the jumping latch before setting `Status_InAir` for knockback. This matches S1 `HurtSonic`, S2 `HurtCharacter`/`Tails_ResetOnFloor_Part2`, and S3K `HurtCharacter`/`Player_TouchFloor` (`docs/s1disasm/_incObj/Sonic ReactToItem.asm:390-392`, `docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:85468-85471,41033-41037`, `docs/skdisasm/sonic3k.asm:21090-21093,24365-24369`). `TestS2Cnz2LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f9733 / 301 errors (`tails_status_byte` expected `0x0002`, actual `0x0012`) to f9946 / 300 errors (`x_speed` expected `0x0200`, actual `0x08A8`).
- **S2 OOZ2 Obj07 oil support now skips CPU Tails dead-fall routine 6:** `OilSurfaceManager` now treats the S2 sidekick `DEAD_FALLING` state as the ROM Obj02_Dead routine for manager-hosted Obj07 oil support, clearing stale support instead of re-seating Tails on the boss-lowered oil plane before `obj_control` becomes negative. This matches `PlatformObject_ChkYRange` returning when the player routine is `>= 6`; a BizHawk probe over the f9465 window showed Tails routine `$06`, `obj_control=$00`, stale `interact=$0E`, and continuous falling through Obj07 at `$294C,$02D8` (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:35978-35981,50157-50189,41131-41137`). `TestS2Ooz2LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f9465 / 457 errors (`tails_y` expected `0x0299`, actual `0x0298`) to f10129 / 388 errors (`tails_x_speed` expected `0x0000`, actual `0x0200`).
- **S2 ARZ2 Obj37 sidekick collection now uses the ROM main-invulnerability gate:** CPU Tails can now collect spilled Obj37 rings through the same Touch_ChkValue path as the ROM, but the collection threshold reads the main player's `invulnerable_time` before crediting/removing the ring. This matches S2 storing the toucher in `parent(a1)` while gating the branch from `MainCharacter+invulnerable_time`, and preserves MTZ2's hurt-blocking lost-ring window (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:85201-85219,25023-25078`). `TestS2Arz2LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f2142 / 717 errors (`obj_extra_s29_x` expected absent, actual `0x1490`) to f2565 / 713 errors (`obj_s15_slot` expected `0x15`, actual `0x11`); the S2 sweep remains 15 green / 4 expected-red.
- **S2 CNZ2 Obj51 ball trigger now uses the ROM displayed-X phase on leftward passes:** The CNZ boss proximity check now compares Sonic against Obj51's displayed `x_pos(a0)` phase instead of the freshly-moved boss base on the leftward pass. A BizHawk probe at BK2 frame 21917 showed `loc_31BF2` running with `x_pos=$29A2`, `Boss_X_pos=$29A1`, and Sonic `x=$29B1`, making the ROM `dx=$1F` trigger where the engine previously saw `dx=$20` and waited until the ball missed Sonic (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:66577-66594,66658-66664`). `TestS2Cnz2LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f9487 / 288 errors (`g_speed` expected `0x0000`, actual `0x0100`) to f9733 / 301 errors (`tails_status_byte` expected `0x0002`, actual `0x0012`).
- **BizHawk diagnostics now start hidden on the fast launcher path:** `tools\bizhawk\run_bizhawk_lua.bat` now delegates normal no-audio/no-render launches through a hidden PowerShell process wrapper while preserving the generated diagnostic config, fast Lua wrapper, movie/ROM argument order, and the explicit visible-debug escape hatch.
- **S2 OOZ2 Obj55 touch now uses the ROM-visible boss position:** Obj55 exposes the previous object-slot touch position that `Touch_Boss` reads from object RAM before Obj55's next movement step. This lets the post-Obj07 Sonic hurt overlap use the ROM-visible Obj55 body at `$2940,$02BC`, matching `TouchResponse`/`Touch_Boss` and Obj55's dive movement order (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:85021-85022,85164-85255,61282-61295,68330-68359`). `TestS2Ooz2LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f9392 / 476 errors (`x_speed` expected `0x0200`, actual `-0024`) to f9465 / 457 errors (`tails_y` expected `0x0299`, actual `0x0298`).
- **S2 OOZ2 Obj07 hurt oil landings now preserve the ROM hurt-stop handoff:** `OilSurfaceManager` now clears `Status_InAir` for hurt players through the object-hurt landing path instead of immediately clearing the hurt routine. This lets the next `Obj02_Hurt` tick run `Tails_HurtStop`, zero `y_vel`/`x_vel`/`inertia`, and return to routine 2 after Obj07 support, matching the S2 hurt recovery path (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:41063-41118`) while preserving the same landing-frame `RideObject_SetRide` inertia copy. `TestS2Ooz2LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f9342 / 505 errors (`tails_x_sub` expected `0x4700`, actual `0xC700`) to f9392 / 476 errors (`x_speed` expected `0x0200`, actual `-0024`).
- **S2 ARZ2 Obj37 owner allocation now keeps already-freed ROM slots eligible:** Deferred lost-ring materialization now reserves the S2 `HurtCharacter` Obj37 owner from the live allocator state at the hurt instant, so slots deleted earlier in the same `ExecuteObjects` pass remain eligible while later deletes cannot steal the owner slot. This matches `AllocateObject`'s first-empty scan before `Obj37_Init` alternates child-ring velocities (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:33681-33695,85444-85461,25125-25209`). `TestS2Arz2LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f2016 / 753 errors (`obj_extra_s21_x` expected absent, actual `0x1433`) to f2142 / 717 errors (`obj_extra_s29_x` expected absent, actual `0x1490`).
- **S2 OOZ1 Obj48 launcher-ball capture now respects same-pass Obj3D movement ordering:** Obj3D invisible launchers now remember the player's pre-`Obj3D_MoveCharacter` position for the current object pass, and Obj48 defers capture by one pass only when that Obj3D move crossed the player from outside to inside Obj48's 32px capture box. This matches the ROM slot ordering where Obj48's detection pass reads the player's position before the later Obj3D move, then captures on its next pass (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:51176-51188,51306-51315,51341-51352`). `TestS2OozLevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f9342 / 353 errors (`y` expected `0x04CA`, actual `0x04C0`) to green; ARZ2, CNZ2, MTZ3, and OOZ2 preserve their expected-red frontiers.
- **S2 OOZ2 trace routine capture now preserves object-solid hurt landing samples:** trace replay now latches the frame-start hurt-routine state for the narrow case where a sidekick lands on an object/platform and the sampled status still has `Status_OnObj`, while terrain hurt-stop frames can still report routine 2 immediately. This matches S2 `Obj02_Hurt` owning the object-solid landing sample until the next `Obj02_Control` tick, with `Tails_HurtStop` only writing routine 2 when its terrain collision path runs (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:38952-38981,41063-41112`). `TestS2Ooz2LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f9341 / 506 errors (`tails_routine` expected `0x0004`, actual `0x0002`) to f9342 / 505 errors (`tails_x_sub` expected `0x4700`, actual `0xC700`).
- **S2 MTZ3 Obj54 now reserves its ROM SST slot before spawning children:** The MTZ boss event spawn now reserves Obj54's dynamic object slot before the constructor creates its Obj54 laser shooter and Obj53 shield orbs, matching the ROM having Obj54 in `a0` before `Obj54_Init` calls `AllocateObject` for children. Generic dynamic construction keeps its previous semantics so CPZ Obj5D's `AllocateObjectAfterCurrent` child order is not shifted by unrelated transient objects. This restores the S2 `Touch_Loop` SST-order boss hit at the MTZ3 rebound window (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:67224-67240,67782-67808,85048-85058,85191-85201`; CPZ contrast: `docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:61506-61590`). `TestS2Mtz3LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f13054 / 367 errors (`x_speed` expected `0x0091`, actual `-0091`) to f13336 / 352 errors (`x_speed` expected `0x0200`, actual `-0200`) while CPZ2 remains green.
- **S2 OOZ2 Obj55 now preserves the ROM top-level init return before surfacing:** Obj55 construction now stops after the `Obj55_Init` equivalent and defers `Obj55_Main_Init` to the first object update, instead of entering `Obj55_Main_Surface` one object pass early. This keeps the boss body at the ROM-visible `y=$0292` for the f9307 hit before the next hover sample reaches `$0293`, matching the init dispatcher and main-surface/end ordering (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:68225-68238,68258-68276,68287-68301,68355-68359`). `TestS2Ooz2LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f9307 / 430 errors (`y_speed` expected `-0418`, actual `0x0418`) to f9341 / 506 errors (`tails_routine` expected `0x0004`, actual `0x0002`); OOZ1 preserves f9164 / 355.
- **S2 ARZ2 backward placement catch-up now includes the prior left-edge object group:** The post-camera backward placement pass now includes objects whose `x_pos` equals the previous left window edge, matching S2 `ObjectsManager_GoingBackward` after the camera crosses to the new coarse left edge. This lets the ARZ2 `$1400` Obj2C/layer-switcher/monitor cluster stream before slot 23 is freed by Obj8E, preserving the later Obj08 skid-dust slot neighborhood (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:33050-33067`). `TestS2Arz2LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f1998 / 817 errors (`obj_s17_slot` expected `0x17`, actual `0x35`) to f2016 / 753 errors (`obj_extra_s21_x` expected absent, actual `0x1433`).
- **S2 OOZ1 Octus bullets now keep Obj4A's init-facing state:** Obj4A now resolves the ROM one-time init x-flip toggle from MainCharacter position, and `Obj4A_WaitForCharacter` no longer re-faces the Octus before firing. The spawned bullet inherits that stored direction for velocity, letting the OOZ1 CPU Tails hurt touch use the ROM-side `Hurt_Sidekick` rebound direction (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:60391-60430,60481-60505,85468-85484`). `TestS2OozLevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f9164 / 355 errors (`tails_x_speed` expected `0x0200`, actual `-0600`) to f9342 / 353 errors (`y` expected `0x04CA`, actual `0x04C0`).

A rolling hit now latches the Obj53 `collision_property <= -2` equivalent, then the orb advances through its BreakAway/BounceAround/Burst routine updates before `Obj53_Burst` decrements parent `objoff_2C`, matching the ROM's touch-to-object-update handoff (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:67968-68004,68014-68028,68068-68089`). `TestS2Mtz3LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f12897 / 490 errors (`x_speed` expected `-0037`, actual `-0200`) to f13054 / 367 errors (`x_speed` expected `0x0091`, actual `-0091`).

The recorder Lua files also explicitly call `client.SetSoundOn(false)`, and `count_bk2_input_frames.ps1` preserves the BK2 input-frame safety bound previously computed inside the S2/S3K launchers.

Once the marker is gone, `SolidObject_Monitor_Sonic` sees Roll and rejects the landing as ROM does (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:25617-25623,50963-51021,51165-51170,85278-85302`). `TestS2OozLevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f7731 / 490 errors (`y` expected `0x0374`, actual `0x036E`) to f9164 / 355 errors (`tails_x_speed` expected `0x0200`, actual `-0600`).

- **User recording playback now pauses cleanly at level boundaries:** Playback/fast-forward completion policy now runs when gameplay exits through seamless transitions, title-card level loads, respawn fades, act/zone transitions, and credits fades while still classifying the already-applied BK2 frame; the playback HUD also surfaces the live verifier status (`clean`, missing/unsupported/truncated sidecar, or first mismatch) as a non-blocking amber warning when needed.
- **User recording controls are wired into gameplay:** Added configurable `debug.recording.recordKey` support, 60-frame `Shift+Record` hold-to-record in `LEVEL`, plain Record stop for active recordings, master-title `Shift+Record` menu entry, active recording frame feed hooks, playback pause/takeover handling, and bounded fast-forward render suppression with a frame-counter overlay.
- **User recording playback takeover no longer leaks BK2 input:** Ending a paused recording playback through the pause-key takeover now clears the playback session before the forced-input bridge runs on that frame, and the default recording key moved to F9 to avoid the F10 plane-switcher debug overlay.
- **Master-title user recordings menu:** Added a testable recordings menu model and PixelFont text-list screen for browsing per-game BK2 recordings, editing playback target-frame/pause/fast-forward options, showing non-blocking amber version warnings, opening it from the normal master-title flow through a Test Mode-safe Shift+Record seam, and starting playback through the production `UserRecordingSessionLauncher`.
- **User recording launcher can restart and play fresh sessions from recorded context:** Added `UserRecordingSessionLauncher` to capture the current game/zone/act/team/debug launch context, restart the act through a fresh gameplay session, arm recording at movie frame 0 with deterministic `recordings/<game-id>/...bk2` paths, and start manifest-driven playback with desync-lite verifier observation.
- **User recording sessions now own active capture lifecycle and HUD state:** Added the active recording session model that buffers BK2 input frames and desync-lite snapshots, records configured P1/P2 controller lanes with jump mapped to action button A, finalizes recordings through `UserRecordingWriter`, handles abort/IO stop cases, and exposes side-effect-free HUD state/plumbing for later GameLoop wiring.
- **User recording catalog now classifies playback version warnings:** Added a catalog scanner for `recordings/<game-id>/*.bk2` that reads OpenGGF manifests, counts BK2 frames through the playback loader, sorts newest recordings first, and reports non-blocking warnings for missing metadata, dirty builds, official version mismatches, and prerelease build mismatches.
- **User recording desync-lite verifier:** Added the expanded desync-lite snapshot schema, live snapshot capture, configured-main-player resolution, and a playback observer verifier that reports the first comparison mismatch without mutating gameplay state.
- **User recording BK2 writer now emits OpenGGF sidecar entries:** Added `UserRecordingWriter` and `RecordedFrameInput` so engine-authored recordings produce BK2 zip files with `Header.txt`, exact P1/P2 grouped `Input Log.txt`, `OpenGGF/manifest.json`, and `OpenGGF/desync-lite.jsonl` entries that round-trip through `Bk2MovieLoader`.
- **User recording manifests now have stable metadata and JSON codecs:** Added recording launch-context, sidecar, determinism, stop-reason, and manifest models plus a Jackson helper that round-trips `OpenGGF/manifest.json` timestamps without requiring Java-time module support.
- **Build identity metadata now distinguishes prerelease recordings by Git commit:** `version.properties` carries the raw Maven base version plus build-time Git commit and dirty-state fields, and `AppVersion.get()` now displays prerelease builds as `<base>-<commit>` with a `-dirty` suffix when needed while official releases keep the plain base version.
- **Vertical camera boundary clamp is now DIRECTIONAL (top boundary on up-scroll, bottom boundary on down-scroll) instead of a symmetric `[minY, maxY]` clamp — MZ2 GREEN, the last S1 red, so ALL 19/19 S1 complete-run traces are now GREEN:** At MZ2 f13473 the player jumps upward on a ChainedStomper while `DLE_MZ2` eases the bottom level boundary up from `0x520` to `0x200` (camera x just crossed `0x1700`; `f_bgscrollvert`/`maxYChanging` set). The camera was air-tracking up to `camera_y=0x201` (one pixel below the just-eased `v_limitbtm2=0x200`), exactly matching ROM. The engine then unconditionally re-clamped to `[minY, maxY]`, yanking `0x201` -> `0x200` one frame early. ROM's `ScrollVertical` applies the vertical boundaries directionally, like `MoveScreenHoriz`: `SV_MoveCameraUp` -> `SV_TopBoundary` clamps ONLY the top boundary (`v_limittop2`); `SV_MoveCameraDown` -> `SV_BottomBoundary` clamps ONLY the bottom boundary (`v_limitbtm2`); the sweet-spot path clamps the bottom only when `f_bgscrollvert` is set (`SV_BottomBoundaryMoving`) and nothing otherwise (`SV_NoUpdate`) (docs/s1disasm/_inc/`ScrollHoriz & ScrollVertical.asm`:148-261). So the ROM up path never consults the bottom boundary and lets the camera sit transiently below it. Fix: `Camera.updatePosition` now clamps to `minY` when the camera scrolled up, to `maxY` when it scrolled down, and to `maxY` on a no-scroll frame only while `maxYChanging` (the `f_bgscrollvert` mirror) — added `clampTopBoundary`/`clampBottomBoundary`. The change is strictly more ROM-faithful: it only differs from the old symmetric clamp when the camera is beyond the wrong-direction boundary, a state a previously-passing trace cannot contain. Shared cross-game camera code, no zone/route/frame carve-out. Zero regression: all 19 S1 `*CompleteRunTraceReplay` (now incl. MZ2) + 8 S1 credits demos + S2 EHZ1 + `TestCamera` (26) + `TestRewindCoverageGuard` + `TestArchitecturalSourceGuard` GREEN; S3K AIZ/HCZ complete-run frontiers unchanged (identical pre-existing error counts before/after).
- **S1 Moving Block (`Obj0x52`) ridden-bounds walk-off now uses the block's pre-move x, fixing a missed 1-frame airborne on an oscillating block — MZ2 frontier f8661 -> f13473 (665 -> 1 error); full S1 sweep + S2 EHZ1 + guards held GREEN:** The player rides a horizontally-oscillating Moving Block (`Obj0x52`, type 01); ROM clears `Status_OnObj` at f8660 (the player reaches the block's right edge) and goes airborne for one frame at f8661 before re-landing at f8662. The engine walked off one frame late, so it re-landed instead of ever going airborne (`air` mismatch exp=1 act=0). Cause: ROM `MBlock_StandOn` (routine 4) runs `ExitPlatform` — the walk-off bounds check — BEFORE `MBlock_Move`, observing the block's PRE-move x_pos (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/`52 Moving Blocks.asm`:64-83; `sub ExitPlatform.asm`:24-29), while the engine moves the block in `update()` before the solid checkpoint and checked bounds against the POST-move x. Fix: `Sonic1MovingBlockObjectInstance.usesPreUpdatePositionForSolidContact` returns true only while the queried player is already riding this block, so the continued-ride bounds check uses the pre-move x (matching `ExitPlatform`) while a fresh landing keeps the post-move x (routine 2 `MBlock_Platform` runs `MBlock_Move` before `PlatformObject`, Moving Blocks.asm:55-61). The pinned osc-phase theory was disproven by a per-frame `OscillationManager` vs `v_oscillate` aux diff (byte-perfect at f8661). Comparison-only, object-local, S1-only, no zone/route/frame carve-out. Zero regression: all 18 other S1 `*CompleteRunTraceReplay` green + S2 EHZ1 + `TestRewindCoverageGuard` + `TestArchitecturalSourceGuard` green; MZ2 remains the only S1 red, now at f13473 (a separate single-frame 1px camera-vertical-scroll root).
- **S1 Caterkiller fragment-mode off-screen delete now clears the respawn bit, fixing a missed MZ2 Basaran bounce — MZ2 frontier f4610 -> f8661 (824 -> 665 errors); full S1 sweep + S2 EHZ1 held GREEN:** When the player frag-hit a Caterkiller (`Obj0x78`) body segment, the head entered fragment mode and bounced off-screen; `Sonic1CaterkillerBadnikInstance.updateFragment` deleted it with `setDestroyed(true)` (non-respawnable), which left the REV01 `bset` placement counter bit latched so the layout entry never respawned the Caterkiller when the camera returned. ROM `Cat_Fragment` `.displayOrDelete` routes an off-screen fragment to `Cat_Despawn`, which does `bclr #7,2(a2,d0.w)` to CLEAR the `v_objstate` respawn bit before `DeleteObject` (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/`78 Badnik - Caterkiller.asm`:206-208,139-148) — a RememberState off-screen unload, not a permanent kill. Fix: the fragment off-screen branch now calls `setDestroyedByOffscreen()` (respawnable; clears the placement counter bit). The MZ2 `@0x200` Caterkiller now respawns at f3031 (slots 39/41/42/52) as ROM does, so the f4019 scattered-ring spill lands in ROM slots [35,39,41] not [35,54,58], the Basaran (`Obj0x55`) takes slot 40 not 39, its vblank drop-gate `(v_vblank+d7)&7` (d7=127−slot) fires on ROM's frame, and the f4610 bounce registers. Comparison-only, object-local, S1-only, no zone/route/frame carve-out. Zero regression: full S1 `*TraceReplay` sweep (19 green incl MZ1/MZ3/SBZ) + S2 EHZ1 + `TestRewindCoverageGuard` + `TestArchitecturalSourceGuard` green; MZ2 remains the only S1 red, now at f8661 (a separate SwingingPlatform `Obj0x15` ride slot-cadence root).
- **S1 MZ lava-geyser eruption period now ROM-exact, fixing the MZ2 lavafall body-column hurt -- MZ2 frontier f2823 -> f4610 (1116 -> 824 errors); MZ1/MZ3 held GREEN:** The MZ lava-geyser eruption schedule drifted one *executed* frame earlier per cycle (ROM period 255, engine 254), so by the 5th eruption the lavafall body column (`Obj0x4D`, `col_hurt`) arrived ~4 frames early and missed the player overlap at f2823 (`x_speed` exp 0x0200 act 0x0000). RAM ground truth (the trace's `object_appeared`/`object_near objoff_32` aux) disproved the "maker respawns early" theory: the maker (`Obj0x4C`) respawns and first-erupts at the ROM-correct frames; the drift was an animation-timing accumulation. Three ROM-cited fixes: (A) `Sonic1LavaGeyserObjectInstance` drops the `ranGeyserMainThisFrame` head-deferral because `Geyser_Main` falls through to `Geyser_Action` on the spawn frame (no rts; docs/s1disasm/_incObj/`4C, 4D MZ Lava Geyser and Maker.asm`:157/206/235); (B) `Sonic1LavaGeyserMakerObjectInstance.updateAnimation` is rewritten to match `AnimateSprite` exactly via a `subq.b #1,obTimeFrame; bpl Anim_Wait` countdown (docs/s1disasm/_incObj/`sub AnimateSprite.asm`) -- the old version held the first frame for `speed` instead of `speed+1` calls, firing every `afRoutine` one frame early, which under-counted the maker's `.bubble3` rt8->A advance by one frame per eruption (speed constants switched to the raw ROM script bytes from docs/s1disasm/_anim/`Lava Geyser.asm`); (C) the push-block-spawned maker constructor's `timer=1` seed (which had been compensating fix B's off-by-one) becomes the ROM-faithful `timer=0`, so the MZ3 push-block geyser no longer fires one frame late. The original f2823 hurt now lands; MZ2 advances to f4610, a separate Basaran badnik (`Obj0x55`) bounce. Comparison-only, no zone/route/frame carve-out. Zero regression: full S1 `*TraceReplay` sweep = 18 green (incl MZ1+MZ3) + S2 EHZ1 + S3K must-keeps + `TestRewindCoverageGuard` + `TestArchitecturalSourceGuard` green; MZ2 remains the only S1 red.
- **S2 ARZ2 Obj2C leaves generator now uses ROM touch latches and frame phasing:** `LeavesGeneratorObjectInstance` now participates in the S2 special `Touch_Loop` path via Obj2C's `collision_flags`/`collision_property` bits instead of a main-player-only manual rectangle, alternates the main/sidekick leaf checks through Obj2C's saved `Level_frame_counter` phase, and preserves the REV01 `FixBugs=0` child-angle typo where spawned leaves start with angle zero (`docs/s2disasm/s2.asm:52046-52123,52126-52182`). `TestS2Arz2LevelSelectTraceReplay#replayMatchesTrace` advances from f643 / 3172 errors (`obj_s11_type` expected `0x2C`, actual missing) to f662 / 3408 errors (`obj_extra_s1E_x` expected absent, actual `0x0749`); the new frontier is downstream leaf child slot/position churn after the first two Obj2C bursts match.

- **S1 SLZ boss defers its defeat-routine dispatch by one frame, fixing the boss-escape camera-boundary timing — SLZ3 GREEN (4@f12784 -> 0 errors, 18th S1 green):** The SLZ boss defeat->exit-jump->escape timeline ran one frame early, so the escape boundary scroll (`addq.w #2,(v_limitright2)` via `runCameraExpandEscape`) opened one frame too soon (`camera_x` exp 0x2000 act 0x2002 at f12784, with the f12932 x/x_speed/g_speed cascade flowing from it).
